**Bottom line:** I found no company-specific news behind Monday's drop. It looks like a crypto-sector selloff plus a weakening story, and no sign of a turn yet. After about eight searches and eight page opens, the later searches mostly repeated earlier results. Several sources conflict, and I flag those below.

**What happened Monday and over the last two weeks**
- **Monday's move:** The stock opened at $57.67 against a $62.20 Friday close and closed near $57.65. One source puts the close at $57.88, a small discrepancy. [MarketBeat](https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/price-circle-internet-group-nyse-crcl-shares-gap-down-following-insider-selling-2026-11-16/), [GuruFocus](https://www.gurufocus.com/news/9158193/circle-internet-group-crcl-shares-fall-56-after-usdc-freeze-amid-binance-security-breach)
- **Crypto backdrop:** Bitcoin fell as low as about $64,000 Monday. It is down about 16% for November (the second-worst start since 2016) and about 25% year to date. Coinbase and Strategy fell about 5% and Robinhood about 3% in early trading; premarket moves of 7-8% were also reported for Coinbase, Circle and Strategy. [Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/bitcoins-november-rout-echoes-past-crypto-downturns-142926241.html), [cryptonews.net](https://cryptonews.net/news/analytics/33759067/)
- **Why crypto is weak:** The cited causes are expected Fed tightening, miner selling, the CLARITY Act failing to advance, and the Binance hack. The same article notes a less friendly Democratic majority after the midterms. Monday was also a risk-off day: the Nasdaq fell over 2% as Nvidia led AI stocks lower. [Yahoo live blog](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/live/stock-market-today-monday-november-16-dow-sp-500-nasdaq-nvidia-oil-091631084.html)
- **Insider sales, minor:**
  - Director Ostling sold 1,500 shares at $64.74, about $97k.
  - Nikhil Chandhok sold 26,668 shares at $66.09, about $1.76M, under a pre-arranged 10b5-1 plan. He still holds 708k shares.
  - The size is small, so I would treat these as noise.
- **Prior days:**
  - Friday's close was $62.20, down 2.5%.
  - The close was $67.56 on Nov 9.
  - One source says the stock is down about 24% since the Nov 4 earnings. [Coin Republic](https://www.thecoinrepublic.com/2026/11/16/circle-stock-slips-to-62-despite-17-q3-growth/)

**Q3 earnings (Nov 4): a headline beat built on a one-off**
- **Reported numbers:** Revenue was $865M (+17%), adjusted EBITDA $317M (+85%) and EPS $0.84 against a consensus of roughly $0.39-0.42. Guidance was unchanged. [Business Wire via Finviz](https://finviz.com/news/415158/circle-reports-third-quarter-2026-results)
- **The beat came from a token sale:** A $182M recognition from the ARC token presale sits in "other revenue." Excluding it, CoinDesk's AI-generated calculation shows revenue of about $683M (-8%) and adjusted EBITDA of about $135M (-21%). [CoinDesk](https://www.coindesk.com/earnings/crcl-q3-2026-data), [FXC Intelligence](https://www.fxcintel.com/research/analysis/ct-circle-q3-2026-earnings)
- **Core lines weakened:**
  - Reserve income fell 7.5% to $658M.
  - The reserve return rate fell 61 bps to 3.5%.
  - Subscription and services revenue fell 17%, and other revenue excluding the token sale fell 11%.
- **USDC growth has stalled:**
  - Average USDC rose 8% to $73.3B, but period-end USDC was flat year over year at $73.9B.
  - Net issuance was about nil, and USDC's share of stablecoins was flat at 27% (down 2 points year over year).
- **Activity is strong, but not yet revenue:**
  - On-chain volume rose 49%, and mint and redeem volume rose 42%.
  - Circle Payments Network annualized volume reached $41.3B, but fees are not material until 2027.
  - USYC (its tokenized money-market fund) grew to $2.4B.
- **Costs and management:** The company cut about 5% of staff, took a $9.1M restructuring charge, and announced a CFO transition in September. G&A, IT and marketing spending are rising sharply. Q4 guidance implies adjusted opex of $149-164M, up from $139M in Q3.
- **Positives:**
  - Binance invested $100M in equity and renewed the USDC partnership.
  - Arc mainnet launched Sept 16, and the Tazapay deal (about $400M) is due to close in 2027.
  - The GENIUS Act and the OCC's final rule take effect Jan 18, 2027.

**Analysts and valuation**
- **Rating mix:** MarketBeat shows consensus "Hold" with an average target of $91.44, from 2 Strong Buy, 14 Buy, 7 Hold and 5 Sell.
- **Targets cut after earnings:** All three were cut on Nov 5. JPMorgan went to $100 (Overweight), TD Cowen to $87 (Buy) and Susquehanna to $86 (Neutral).
- **Bears:** Morgan Stanley was reported at Underweight with a $38 target (cut from $106 on Aug 3). It cites slowing USDC growth, tokenized money-market funds and deposits eroding balances and take rates, and a shift toward lower-margin transaction revenue. [FXStreet](https://www.fxstreet.com/cryptocurrencies/news/morgan-stanley-cuts-circle-price-target-to-38-as-stablecoin-growth-stirs-concerns-202608040122)
- **Conflict to flag:** One result says Morgan Stanley moved from "underweight" to "cautious" on Nov 5. I could not reconcile this with the August note.
- **Where the price sits:** Market cap is about $14.9B. The 50-day average is about $82.7 and the 200-day about $85.5. The 52-week high of $140 was set May 12.

**Other threads**
- **Binance hack (Oct 29-30):**
  - Circle froze more than $800M of USDC, later cited as about $1.1B. It was criticized for slow freezes in earlier incidents; ZachXBT cited about $420M across 15 cases.
  - The stock fell 5.6% on the day of the freeze (GuruFocus) and about 9% in one day per another search result. I did not fully verify the 9% figure.
  - Binance has set aside about $6.3B to cover losses. [CoinMarketCap](https://coinmarketcap.com/academy/article/circle-froze-1b-usdc-binance-hack), [American Banker](https://www.americanbanker.com/news/6b-binance-heist-provokes-stablecoin-freeze-dilemma)
- **Regulation:**
  - The CLARITY Act passed the Senate Banking Committee 15-9 in May but failed a Senate floor vote (49-50) in September, and is stalled. Polymarket odds of it becoming law in 2026 were about 14% at the time.
  - The fight is over stablecoin yield and rewards. Passing it would help Circle, but nothing is scheduled before the midterm transition. [American Banker](https://www.americanbanker.com/news/crypto-market-structure-bill-fails-in-senate-vote-49-50)
- **Competition:** Coinbase's stablecoin ambitions and its revenue share on USDC reserves weigh on margins. I found nothing specific on Tether's USAT as a near-term threat.
- **Next scheduled event:** Q4 earnings are listed for Feb 24, 2027 by one source, so nothing scheduled falls inside your 1-10 session window. Possible catalysts in the window are bitcoin and crypto-equity direction, Fed and rate expectations, any CLARITY or stablecoin-yield headline, and further insider or Form 4 filings.

**What I could not find or verify**
- No short-interest data.
- No news after the Monday close, and no specific cause for Monday beyond the sector selloff.
- The Block's article and parts of the search summaries were 2025-era content, and several aggregator sites are AI-generated. I relied on the Circle release, CoinDesk, FXC Intelligence, MarketBeat and Yahoo for the main figures.

**Read for the 1-10 session decision**

  - The 50-day is below the 200-day and falling, and the post-earnings downtrend is intact.

**HIMS research as of 12:35 AM CT, Tue 2026-11-17**

**Short version:** HIMS is falling on a bad Q3 report that came after a bad year. Revenue is growing fast, but gross margin has collapsed, subscribers fell for the first time, and profit guidance was cut for the third time in 2026. Management says weak subscriber numbers continue through Q4, with a recovery in Q1. There is no known catalyst in the next 1 to 10 sessions. The stock is oversold, but nothing I found marks a turn.

**What happened (Q3 report, Nov 9 after the close)**
- **Revenue and margins:** Revenue was $890.4M, up 49%, roughly in line. Gross margin fell to 57% from 74% a year earlier, and about 7 points from Q2. The company reported a GAAP net loss of $33.0M and an operating loss of $66.1M. Adjusted EBITDA was $82.4M, a 9% margin versus 13% a year earlier. Free cash flow was $26M versus $79M a year earlier. ([press release](https://investors.hims.com/news/news-details/2026/Hims--Hers-Health-Inc--Reports-Third-Quarter-2026-Financial-Results/default.aspx), [Motley Fool](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/11/16/hims-and-hers-health-stock-crashes-after-earnings-is-now-the-time-to-buy/))
- **Subscribers:** Subscribers were 2.79M, up 13% year over year but down about 100k from Q2. Revenue per subscriber rose 30% to $105.
- **Segments:** US revenue was $657M (+21%). Rest of world was $233M (+321%, mostly acquisitions). International is now about a quarter of revenue and carries lower margins.
- **Guidance:**
  - Q4 revenue is guided to $875–895M, against about $955M expected by analysts.
  - Q4 adjusted EBITDA is guided to $70–90M.
  - Full-year revenue is narrowed to $3.13–3.15B.
  - Full-year adjusted EBITDA was cut to $257–277M from $275–325M.
  - Management cited sharper UK and Germany pricing and marketing, and at least $20M of weight-loss membership revenue shifting into January.
- **Management explanation (earnings call):** The subscriber decline came from deliberately paced US weight-loss marketing while it prepares the Lilly assortment and multi-month subscriptions, plus international brand migrations. They expect at least one more quarter of subscriber headwind, then a Q1 recovery. They also said the pace of margin decline should moderate. A detailed 2027 outlook is promised with the Q4 report. ([call summary](https://uk.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/earnings-call-transcript-hims--hers-misses-q3-2026-profit-view-shares-fall-93CH-4970016))
- **Stock reaction:** The stock fell 11.8% on Nov 9 (to $22.98) ahead of the report, since it was $26.00 before. It then fell about 15–19% intraday on Nov 10, to a seven-month low. Monday's close of $18.56 (-5.9%, 12.1M shares) took it near April's levels. Press accounts disagree on the exact figures for Nov 10 and Nov 16. ([Benzinga](https://www.benzinga.com/analyst-stock-ratings/analyst-color/26/11/63113757/weight-loss-reset-dents-hims-hers-outlook-but-analyst-sees-opportunity), [Invezz](https://invezz.com/news/2026/11/10/hims-hers-stock-plunges-19-after-q3-loss-and-weaker-subscriber-growth/), [Trefis](https://www.trefis.com/stock/hims/articles/624992/should-hims-hers-stocks-drop-after-earnings-worry-you/2026-11-13))
- **Drift since:** Coverage after Nov 10 mostly cites the subscriber decline. I found no distinct Monday news item beyond that.

**Background story**
- **Novo suit:** Novo sued over compounded semaglutide on Feb 9, and the stock fell 18% that day. On Mar 9 Hims said it would stop advertising compounded GLP-1s, mainly sell FDA-approved GLP-1s, and add Wegovy and Ozempic. Novo dropped the case without prejudice, so it can refile. ([CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/02/09/novo-nordisk-sues-hims-hers-compounded-obesity-drugs.html), [10-Q](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001773751/000177375126000246/hims-20260930.htm)). The business has shifted from high-margin compounded drugs to lower-margin branded ones. That is the main cause of the margin collapse.
- **Lilly deal (Nov 6):** Zepbound (from $299 a month) and Foundayo (the oral drug orforglipron, from $149 a month) will be sold on the platform. Hims committed never to offer compounded copies of Lilly's drugs. The stock rose about 7–8% on the news, and that gain has since been lost. ([Morningstar/Business Wire](https://www.morningstar.com/news/business-wire/20261106567564/lilly-and-hims-hers-expand-access-to-fda-approved-lilly-medicines), [Fierce Healthcare](https://www.fiercehealthcare.com/health-tech/hims-hers-inks-deal-eli-lilly-offer-branded-weight-loss-drugs))
- **FTC suit and class action:** The FTC sued on Jul 29, alleging subscription billing and cancellation violations (ROSCA) and deceptive advertising, with Utah and Los Angeles County as co-plaintiffs. The complaint also alleges health data was shared with Meta and Snap. The stock fell 14.7% to $25.00 that day. A securities class action covers purchases from Aug 4, 2025 to Jul 29, 2026 (lead-plaintiff deadline was Nov 2). Company says a loss is not probable. Most coverage of this comes from law-firm solicitations, and I found no ruling or settlement. ([law-firm page](https://robbinsllp.com/hims-hers-health/), [complaint](https://www.courthousenews.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/hims-securities-complaint.pdf))
- **Acquisitions and debt:**
  - It bought Zava and Eucalyptus (reported at up to $1.15B), which brings international to $650M or more of 2026 revenue.
  - The $350M 0% convertible notes due 2032 convert at about $29.53, far above the current price. ([BusinessWire](https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260518180060/en/Hims-Hers-Health-Inc.-Prices-Upsized-%24350-Million-Convertible-Senior-Notes-Offering-to-Support-International-Expansion-and-Accelerate-AI-Driven-Platform-Investment), [Fierce](https://www.fiercehealthcare.com/telehealth/hims-hers-acquires-european-health-tech-company-zava-all-cash-deal))
  - The Q3 balance sheet shows $712M of cash and short-term investments against $1.37B of convertible notes and a $479M current deferred acquisition payable. Equity is only $355M, and goodwill is $1.11B. Free cash flow for the year to date is just $10.8M.
- **Peptides and testosterone:**
  - Peptides+ (sermorelin, glutathione, NAD+) launches in late November, with only minor Q4 revenue expected. BPC-157 and TB-500 wait on FDA rules, which management expects "in a few weeks." The regulatory status of those two is unclear and the sources conflict.
  - Testosterone therapy (its first controlled substances) has launched.

**Analysts and sentiment**
- **Post-Q3 targets:** Needham cut to $32 from $42 and kept Buy. Jefferies cut to $24 from $31 and kept Hold. Canaccord kept Buy with a $40 target. Consensus target is about $31, but most of the 15 analysts covering it rate it Hold. Jefferies warned of "heightened stock gyrations." ([Stocktwits/Jefferies](https://stocktwits.com/news-articles/markets/equity/hims-may-see-heightened-gyrations-as-weight-loss-drug-trends-fuel-subscriber-uncertainty-jefferies/cNGuVH4R9J7), [TIKR](https://www.tikr.com/blog/hims-hers-has-lost-53-of-its-value-in-a-year-canaccord-still-sees-40))
- **Retail:** Retail sentiment on Stocktwits spiked to "extremely bullish" after the drop, with people calling it a buy zone. That is a contrarian caution rather than a signal.
- **Short interest:** The latest I found was about 23.6% of float (54.9M shares, 4.3 days to cover) as of Sep 17, falling from over 30% in July. I found no post-earnings figure. A squeeze is possible, but I can't confirm the setup.
- **Insiders:** Insider sales in 2026 appear to be small, routine, and 10b5-1 or RSU-tax related. I found no November open-market buys or buyback announcement.

**Next 1 to 10 sessions**
- **Scheduled catalysts:** I found none. Q4 results come around February. Possible unscheduled items:
  - FDA peptide rulings
  - Peptides+ launch in late November
  - FTC litigation developments
  - Novo refiling
  - Lilly and Novo product news
  - Insider Form 4s
- **Valuation:** Market cap is about $4.35B on roughly $3.1B of revenue, so it is cheap on sales. But EBITDA is thin, GAAP profit is negative, and debt is meaningful.
- **Possible rebound argument:** The stock is down about 34% in 20 days, the selling was on low volume Monday (0.8x normal), and the 52-week low of $13.74 is well below.
- **Why not to lean on it:** Weak subscriber data is guided for Q4 and the legal overhang is unresolved. A $4.5B stock priced near $18.5 has no obvious catalyst, so a bounce could fade.

**Gaps and caveats**
- The Nov 16 close is from Motley Fool ($18.56, matches your data). Another outlet's $19.08 close looks wrong.
- Several secondary sources (Stocktwits, Substack, tiny news aggregators) conflict on details. The 10-Q and press release are the reliable ones.
- I did not open the full 10-Q text or find any Tuesday pre-market news.

# What the US market is arguing about (as of 12:35 AM CT, Tue Nov 17, 2026)

All figures come from secondary web reports that sometimes disagree. I note conflicts where they matter. I found no coverage yet of Tuesday's overnight trading.

## Monday's tape
- **Indexes:** The S&P 500 fell 1.9% to about 7,417, its third straight loss and its biggest one-day drop since Nov 5. The Nasdaq Composite fell 2.5% to 24,510, which is about 11% below its Oct 6 high and counts as a correction. The Dow fell 1.4% to about 51,608.
- **Breadth:** 355 of 500 S&P stocks fell. Only Consumer Staples and Utilities rose. Technology fell 3.2%.
- **Chips:** The semiconductor ETFs SOXX and SMH fell 5%, Micron fell 7.6%, AMD 5.6%, Broadcom 3.9% and Oracle 5%. Taiwan's Taiex fell 6%, with TSMC down 5.7%, and Korea's Kospi fell 3.6%.
- **Fear gauges:** The VIX rose to about 23, and the Nasdaq-100 volatility index (VXN) closed at its 98th percentile for the past year. The QQQ (Nasdaq-100 ETF) closed below its 200-day average.
- **Context:** The week before, the S&P 500 had its first weekly gain after a four-week losing streak, so Monday partly reversed that rebound.

## The main stories

**1. Nvidia is in a leadership and legitimacy crisis, and reports tonight.**
- Jensen Huang resigned as CEO and director around Nov 12. Reports link this to revelations about extramarital affairs, one involving a former Megaspeed executive that US intelligence suspects of spying for China. Megaspeed is a Singapore firm suspected of diverting Nvidia chips to China.
- CFO Colette Kress is interim CEO. Nvidia shares have lost more than $1 trillion in market value since late October, by two outlets' estimates.
- Treasury Secretary Bessent called for a "dramatic shakeup" and an outside CEO. He also questioned whether Nvidia's Singapore revenue surge was diverted chips and said other executives should face scrutiny.
- Trump and Musk would welcome Huang's return, and a petition has more than 150,000 signatures. A source told CNBC the board is not discussing it. The Financial Times reportedly says the board approached Arm CEO Rene Haas.
- Bessent also reportedly pressed Commerce Secretary Lutnick over not blacklisting Megaspeed, which Commerce denies. The Commerce Department has since closed a loophole that let Chinese firms rent US AI chips abroad.
- Nvidia stock closed at $156, its lowest since June 2025 and down roughly 24-39% depending on the starting point. Mizuho cut its target to $220, UBS to $240 and HSBC to $170.
- Nvidia reports after the close tonight (about 3:20 PM CT; the call is at 4:00 PM CT). Consensus is roughly $109-111B revenue and about $2.47-2.52 EPS. Previews say guidance and management tone on customer budgets matter more than the headline numbers. The bull case is a forward P/E under 13 and hyperscaler capex above $1 trillion in 2027. Whether the printed revenue is clean and whether the Singapore question gets answered are open risks.

**2. Is AI spending peaking?**
- Over the weekend, SemiAnalysis cut its 2028 AI accelerator spending forecast 28% to $758B and its 2030 forecast 40% to $923B. It cited slowing revenue growth at AI labs, tighter financing, construction delays and price deflation. Asian markets reacted first, then US chips. This is secondary reporting; I did not find the original report.
- A related thread is that AI is now a credit story. Fed Governor Bowman warned this week that AI-related debt could pass $800B and mentioned circular financing. UBS puts off-balance-sheet hyperscaler commitments near $3.5T. Hyperscaler bond spreads have roughly doubled over the past year. Dell fell 7% after an industry debt warning, though I could not confirm the details.
- One counterpoint is JPMorgan Asset Management's view that the spread widening reflects heavy supply, not weaker businesses. Earnings strength is another: FactSet shows Q3 S&P earnings up about 32%, but a few AI names, led by Nvidia and Micron, drive much of it, and the average beat margin is small.

**3. The Fed is expected to hike in December (a surprise relative to the old rate-cut narrative).**
- October CPI rose 0.4% overall and 0.3% in core, both above forecasts. October PPI was up 6.5% from a year earlier, the most since Nov 2022, with core PPI up 0.5%.
- The Fed under Chair Kevin Warsh raised rates to 3.75%-4.00% in September and held in October. Markets price about a 90% chance of a quarter-point hike on Dec 9, with 6-14% for a half-point (sources disagree on the exact figure). Waller said core CPI at about 0.3% puts a half-point on the table. January and March hikes are priced at about 65% each.
- The 10-year Treasury yield is around 5.1% and the 30-year about 5.46%. The 2-year jumped about 15 basis points on CPI day. The 10-year eased on Monday, which was read as growth worry, not relief.
- October payrolls rose 165,000 against about 59,000 expected, with unemployment at 4.1%.
- Growth is a worry too. The November Empire State manufacturing index was 7.8 against 16.7-18 expected, and new orders collapsed to 3.0. Japan's economy shrank in Q3. The dollar index is at 103.5, its highest since April 2025.

**4. The Anthropic IPO is the next test of AI appetite.**
- Anthropic plans to sell 825M shares at $70-$78 under the ticker ANT, raising up to about $64B. The implied valuation is about $1.3-1.4T on a fully diluted basis, or about $0.9-1.0T on shares outstanding (sources differ). That is below the roughly $2T rumored in September.
- Pricing is Wednesday night (Nov 18) and trading starts Thursday (Nov 19) on Nasdaq. Reports say the book is about six times oversubscribed and banks are weighing pricing above the range.
- The debate is whether a hot debut revives AI risk appetite, or whether a $64B supply of AI stock plus a $900B compute commitment is peak-cycle supply that drains money from other AI names.

**5. Oil and the Iran war.**

**Magnite (MGNI): research for the 1-10 session decision, as of the close on Mon 2026-11-17**

**The story in one paragraph.** Magnite is the largest independent sell-side ad platform. It sells ad space for publishers and streaming TV owners. It has re-rated sharply on three things: streaming TV (CTV) growing about 39%, a political-ad surge, and a favorable Google ad tech ruling. A fourth item, a reported OpenAI/ChatGPT ads tie-up, added a one-day jump. A raised guide and a wave of target raises followed the Nov 4 earnings. The stock is up about 22% in 20 days and about 50% year to date. The price now sits near the pre-ruling analyst target range. The fundamentals are strong. Almost all of the move is already a matter of record, and the known headwinds are 2027 political comps and executive selling.

**Timeline**
- **Sep 2026:** Judge Brinkema's remedies ruling in the Google ad tech case was unsealed around Sep 17. She declined to force a sale of Google's AdX exchange. She ordered behavioral remedies: separating parts of Google's publisher ad server from AdX, real-time bidding access, routing through rival exchanges, and a six-year monitor. MGNI rose as much as 12.9% that day. StoneX raised its target to $43 from $33, and Craig-Hallum raised its to $32 from $28.
- **Mid-Oct:** The stock was about $23.4 on Oct 16.
- **Nov 2:** The Information reported that OpenAI struck unannounced deals with Magnite and PubMatic to fill remnant ChatGPT ad inventory. Volumes are described as modest but expected to grow fast. MGNI rose about 5% that day. Another source says about 13%, so the size is unconfirmed.
- **Nov 4, Q3 results.**
  - Revenue was $204.2M (+14%) and adjusted EPS was $0.33, a beat.
  - Contribution ex-TAC (revenue after traffic acquisition costs) was $200.6M (+20%).
  - CTV was $105.4M (+39%), above the $98-100M guide. CTV is 53% of the total.
  - The stock jumped about 11.5% to roughly $25.4.
- **Nov 9 and 11:** Several executives and a director sold about 92,000 shares, about $2.7M, per MarketBeat-style reports. These are likely routine sales, but they are not purchases. I could not open the details (403 error), so prices, plans and remaining holdings are unverified.
- **Nov 10:** The Trade Desk fell about 7% after its CFO said it does not expect the usual Q3-to-Q4 seasonal lift. PubMatic fell 5%. MGNI held up at about $29.17, and one widget showed $28.79.
- **Nov 16 (Monday):** Your data shows -1.7%. I found no news explaining it, so it looks like ordinary giveback or drift.

**Fundamentals and guidance** (from the call transcript and summaries; I could not open Magnite's own press release, which returned a 403)
- **Q4 guide:**
  - Contribution ex-TAC $227-233M (+16-19%).
  - CTV $124-127M.
  - DV+ (the display and mobile business) $103-106M.
  - Adjusted EBITDA margin 44-46%.
- **Full-year 2026:**
  - Contribution ex-TAC growth about 17% (was 13-14%).
  - Adjusted EBITDA growth about 30% (was above 20%).
  - Margin about 38.5%.
  - Free cash flow growth above 60%.
- **Political ads:**
  - Q3 was about $12M, over 75% of it CTV.
  - The full-year guide is above $40M, up from $15M.
  - Management expects Q4 political to exceed Q3. It will be over 5% of 2026 contribution ex-TAC, against 2-3% in past cycles.
- **2027 initial outlook:**
  - Growth above 15% excluding political, or above 10% reported.
  - Adjusted EBITDA margin of at least 38.5%.
  - The guide excludes any Google remedy upside.
  - Management admitted political spend crowded out other advertising in some markets, and that the speed of recovery for non-political budgets is unclear.
- **CTV drivers:**
  - Top-10 accounts grew in the mid-40% range, and other partners grew above 30%.
  - Named strong partners were Disney/ESPN, Fox/Tubi, LG Ads, Netflix, Roku, Skydance and Vizio/Walmart.
  - Live sports is now a major programmatic contributor.
  - International CTV is growing as streamers launch in new markets.
  - LG Ad Solutions signed a three-year exclusive SpringServe extension. Pinterest named Magnite its primary SSP, and HP TV+ chose it as primary video ad server.
  - Management calls the 25% long-term CTV growth target aspirational.
- **DV+:** Roughly flat to low-single-digit growth. Mobile in-app grew 17%. Open-web traffic is under pressure from search and referral changes.
- **Balance sheet and buybacks:**
  - Cash was $393M, and the company is in a net cash position (leverage -0.2x).
  - The term loan was repriced to SOFR + 2.5%.
  - It bought back about $29M of stock in Q3 and about $86M year to date, with about $145M authorized and remaining.
  - Buybacks are a supportive bid on dips.

**Analysts**
- Ten Buy ratings and two Hold, per MarketBeat-style reports.
- Targets after earnings:
  - Susquehanna $35, up from $30.
  - BTIG $33, up from $27.
  - Scotiabank and RBC $30, up from $27.
  - Wells Fargo $23, up from $22, equal-weight.
- Earlier targets were StoneX $43 and Craig-Hallum $32.
- The stock at $28.5-28.8 is above two of the four post-earnings targets I found with exact prices and close to the others. It is at or above the Scotiabank, RBC and Wells Fargo targets and below BTIG, Susquehanna and StoneX. Upside to consensus is thin, but the bulls are well above the price.
- Valuation is conflicting: MarketScreener shows about 10x 2027 EV/EBITDA, and a Substack post says about 13x. That is cheap to moderate for 30%-growth EBITDA, but it is not distressed.

**Risks and open questions**
- **Google final judgment.**
  - The parties filed a proposed joint final judgment on Oct 2. I found no confirmation that one has been entered.
  - Conduct rules reportedly take effect 60 days after entry, and Google plans to appeal.
  - Google estimates 12-18 months for the technical work, and the industry estimates 6-12 months.
  - A final order could land during your window and would be headline-sensitive in either direction. Today the benefit is mostly priced in as hope.
- **2027 political cliff.** Reported growth guides to only about 10%. The first 2027 quarters will face a hard comparison.
- **Ad-tech sentiment.** The Trade Desk's seasonality warning and large-advertiser softness (consumer goods, autos) are a read-through risk. MGNI held up on Nov 10 but is a high-beta peer.
- **Insider selling** in the 92k-share range, small against the roughly $4.2B market cap.
- **Open-web weakness** in DV+, and agentic and AI-search shifts.
- **OpenAI deal** is unannounced and sourced to one report. Treat any upside as unconfirmed.

**Catalysts in or near the window**
- Raymond James conference Dec 8, Wells Fargo TMT Dec 9, Susquehanna session Dec 14, Needham Jan 13. These are mostly outside the 1-10 session window, apart from possible pre-conference commentary.
- Possible Google final judgment entry.
- No earnings until late February.
- Possible OpenAI announcements.

**What I could not verify**
- Magnite's own press release and the insider details (403 errors).
- Current short interest. The only figures I found were stale (7.3% about a year ago, 14% in March 2025).
- Any news on Nov 16-17.

**Read for the decision.** The momentum is fundamentally backed: a guidance raise, CTV beats, a net cash balance sheet, a buyback and a favorable legal backdrop. But the screen's setup is a +22% run with no turn yet, and targets are near the price. The news flow into the window is quiet apart from the unscheduled Google final order, so there is no obvious scheduled catalyst. # What the US market is arguing about, as of 12:35 AM CT Tue Nov 17, 2026

**Monday's close:** The S&P 500 fell 1.92% to 7,416.59, its third straight loss. The Nasdaq fell 2.49% to 24,509.76, about 10.9% below its Oct 6 high, which is correction territory. The Dow fell 1.41% to 51,608. The VIX rose about 19% to roughly 22.9. Only about 145 S&P names rose. Sources: [WTOP/AP](https://wtop.com/national/2026/11/how-major-us-stock-indexes-fared-monday-11-16-2026), [Motley Fool](https://www.fool.com/coverage/stock-market-today/2026/11/16/stock-market-today-nov-16-tech-selloff-deepens-as-ai-leadership-crisis-rattles-nasdaq/), [Yahoo live blog](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/live/stock-market-today-monday-november-16-dow-sp-500-nasdaq-nvidia-oil-091631084.html).

## The six stories, ranked by how much they are moving prices

### 1. Nvidia without Jensen Huang, and its earnings tonight (the main story)
- **Why Huang left:** He resigned Nov 12 after reports of affairs, one involving a woman reportedly suspected of working for Chinese intelligence. CFO Colette Kress is interim CEO. Sources: [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/12/nvidia-jensen-huang-ceo-live-updates.html), [Al Jazeera](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/12/why-did-nvidia-ceo-jensen-huang-resign-and-who-is-colette-kress).
- **The "bring him back" fight:**
  - A petition has reportedly drawn 180,000 signatures. Elon Musk signed it, and Trump said he "would not mind" a return.
  - On Monday CNBC reported the board is not considering it, and NVDA fell about 4% to session lows.
  - The FT says Huang has talked with confidants about returning. Rene Haas (Arm) and Tim Cook have been floated as successors.
  - Sources: [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/16/nvidia-ceo-jensen-huang.html), [CBS](https://www.cbsnews.com/news/jensen-huang-nvidia-ceo-reinstatement-petition/).
- **The stock:** It is reportedly down about 13% over five days.
- **The setup:** Nvidia reports fiscal Q3 after the close tonight.
  - Consensus is about $108.7B revenue and $2.47 EPS.
  - Q4 revenue guidance is the real test, with consensus about $124.8B. Goldman expects a beat and raise, and BofA puts a 60% chance on one.
  - Options imply roughly an 8-10% move. Nvidia has guided above consensus in four straight quarters, yet the stock fell after three of them.
  - Sources: [SpotGamma](https://spotgamma.com/nvidia-earnings-preview-leadership-shock/), [Yahoo/options](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/options/articles/nvidia-q3-earnings-preview-options-205720323.html), [Investing.com](https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/nvidia-earnings-scenarios-what-a-guidance-cut-could-mean-for-the-stock-93CH-5030809).
- **The argument:** One side says a strong print with a steady-hand call, or a credible CEO announcement, relieves a stock that is already washed out. The other side says governance, China-espionage and export-control risk deserve a lasting discount even if the numbers are fine.

### 2. The Fed may hike, and bond yields are the macro lid
- **Policy path:** This is a tightening cycle, not a cutting one. Markets price a December 9 hike at roughly 89-100%. Core CPI has risen 0.3% three months in a row, which is exactly Governor Waller's bar for considering 50 bp. About 9-14% is priced for a half-point move, and sources disagree on that figure. Sources: [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/13/treasury-yields-fed-rates.html), [MLQ](https://mlq.ai/news/october-cpi-runs-hotter-than-expected-as-core-inflation-hits-wallers-threshold-for-a-half-point-hike/), [Axios](https://www.axios.com/2026/11/10/cpi-october-inflation-fed).
- **Yields:** The 10-year is about 5.15% (it hit 5.17% intraday Friday), the 30-year about 5.47%, and the 2-year about 4.86%. Last week was the biggest yield jump in about 19 months.
- **Producer prices:** PPI is up 6.5% over 12 months, the most since Nov 2022, and core PPI rose 0.5% in October. Bulls on yields call this transitory goods inflation, while bears see a pipeline into consumer prices.
- **Fed speakers this week:** Warsh spoke Monday on AI and productivity and avoided inflation and policy, so that was no help to markets. October FOMC minutes come Wednesday, and Waller, Williams, Hammack, Kashkari and Barr are also scheduled to speak.
- **Data caveat:** The BLS has no 12-month CPI for October because of last year's shutdown gap, so inflation readings are noisier than usual.
- **Why it matters for stocks:** The S&P forward P/E is reportedly about 18.7 against a 5%+ risk-free rate. Long-duration growth is the most exposed.

### 3. Is the AI buildout being financed too aggressively?
- **Bowman's warning:** Fed Governor Michelle Bowman said AI-related debt (bonds, private credit, project finance) is heading above $800B this year, with lease and guarantee commitments possibly several times that. She flagged "circular financing" among hyperscalers, chipmakers and smaller firms, and the risk of a large equity correction if returns disappoint. Sources: [Fool](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/11/16/fed-governor-michelle-bowman-risk-of-large-correction-in-stocks-if-ai-doesn-t-pan-out/), [MLQ](https://mlq.ai/news/feds-bowman-warns-of-a-stock-correction-if-ai-bets-dont-pay-off-and-says-there-is-still-work-to-do-on-inflation/).
- **Credit signals:**
  - Oracle has the widest spreads among hyperscalers and is the only one downgraded or on negative outlook. Meta is next. These are secondary sources.
  - Dell fell about 7% on Monday on industrywide debt worries. Its debt is about $35B, up from about $29B a year earlier.
  - Sources: [LSEG](https://www.lseg.com/en/insights/ftse-russell/ais-borrowing-boom-what-it-means-for-bond-indices), [Yahoo](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/stock-market-news-nov-16-222502139.html).
- **The two camps:**
  - Bulls say hyperscalers can earn about 15% returns on capital, with Goldman and Morgan Stanley comfortable with top-tier paper.
  - Bears say capex now exceeds operating cash flow, Alphabet's Q3 free cash flow was reportedly negative, and Burry argues depreciation is understated.
  - Capex estimates range from about $660B to $800B for 2026 and $1.1-1.3T for 2027. Those come from commentary and aggregators.

### 4. The Anthropic IPO as a market event
- **Terms:**
  - Ticker ANT on Nasdaq, priced Wed night, trading Thursday Nov 19.
  - Range is $70-78 for 825M shares, raising up to about $64B.
  - Valuation is up to about $1.4T fully diluted, against $965B in May and earlier talk near $2T.
  - The book is reportedly covered. Retail allocation is about 20%. Google, Nvidia and others take $26B of non-voting stock.
  - Sources: [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/16/anthropic-ipo-date-price-range.html), [Fool](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/11/13/anthropic-set-its-ipo-price-range-at-70-to-78-valuing-it-at-up-to-1405-trillion/), [Fortune](https://fortune.com/2026/11/10/anthropic-ipo-price-range-ai-stock-sell-off/).
- **The arguments:**
  - **Liquidity:** Vanda estimates retail net buying of about $250M on day one, more than double SpaceX's June record, and some of it may be funded by selling other AI stocks. Some call the mega-IPO wave a supply glut or a top signal (Burry). Yardeni calls the drain fears overblown.
  - **Read-through:** Amazon and Alphabet each own more than 5% of Anthropic. Nvidia is both an investor and a competitor for AI wallet share. A strong debut would validate AI economics, and a weak one would hit sentiment.
  - **Pipeline:** BofA's CEO says other listings are being pushed to 2027. OpenAI is still to come.

### 5. Chip export controls, and the China and security angle
- **The rule:** A Commerce interim rule (around Nov 15) requires licenses for advanced AI chips going to Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Brazil, aimed at diversion to China. Sources: [Cryptobriefing](https://cryptobriefing.com/amd-stock-slides-chip-export-restrictions/), [Yahoo](https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/articles/amd-mu-skhy-avgo-chip-040420540.html).
- **Monday's moves:** AMD fell about 5.6% to $504, and Intel fell 7-9% after a class action suit. Intel was already down 28.6% after October's earnings. SMH or SOX fell roughly 3-5%, depending on the source. The Nvidia espionage story overlaps with this theme.
- **Trump and Musk in Asia:** Trump travels to Asia this week and Musk joins the China leg, so any trade or chip headline could land at any time.

### 6. Consumer and housing under a 5% 10-year
- **Housing:** Home Depot reports before the open today (consensus about $3.86 EPS on $42.7B). Management called housing "frozen" in August, so the question is whether pro demand offsets it.
- **Retail sales:** October retail sales are also due today, with consensus +0.2% after +0.8% in September.
- **Retailers:** Target reports Wed (about $2.04 EPS), and Walmart Thu (about $0.64 EPS on about $187B). Last quarter's Target EPS included a $994M tariff refund, so the quality of earnings is under scrutiny. Walmart trades around 45x earnings against Target at about 17x.
- **Other earnings:** Palo Alto Networks and Disney also report this week. Sources: [Yahoo](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/expect-markets-week-nvda-panw-102428642.html), [StoneX](https://www.stonex.com/en-gb/news-and-analysis/equities-weekly-outlook-walmart-home-depot-and-target/).

## Secondary threads
- **Rotation to defensives:** Only Staples (+0.3%) and Utilities (+0.2%) closed higher, and Tech was about -3.2%. Real Estate was also reported as outperforming, but sources conflict, as they do on whether Energy was up or down. Tyson Foods rose about 8% on a beat and a better beef outlook.
- **Oil and Iran:**
  - Brent is roughly $92-96 against about $72 before the war began in late February.
  - Iran struck a US base in Bahrain on Sunday, and a third US carrier is heading to the region.

**CHTR (Charter Communications) research, as of 12:35 AM CT Tue 2026-11-17**

**Summary:** The move looks like a sharp relief rally off a washed-out low, not a fundamental turn. The stock sits at about 3x forward earnings with the underlying business still shrinking. The rally has a known catalyst date this week: the $1.5B tender offer expires Nov 17, with settlement expected Nov 19. After that the near-term catalysts thin out, and the next earnings report is not until 2027-01-29.

**How the price got here (sources disagree on some closes, so treat these as approximate)**
- The 52-week low of $101.11 came on Oct 26.
- The stock rose 5.7% on Nov 4 and 4.7% on Nov 5, ahead of earnings.
- Q3 results on Nov 6 sent it down 6.2% to $118.05, its second-largest one-day drop since late August.
- A close near $121 followed on Nov 9.
- On Nov 10 it rose about 10.6% to roughly $134 after the cost plan and the tender offer. The market was down that day, and Comcast barely moved. Altice fell 8% and Cable One fell 15%.
- It was around $138.39 on Nov 13, and your Monday close was 138.95.
- Roughly a 29% gain in a month fits your +28% over 20 sessions.
- Even after this, it is about 23% below its 200-day average and about 45% below the 52-week high of $254.11. One source cites higher figures ($424 to $437), which look stale or mislabeled.

**Q3 results (reported Nov 6)**
- The headline beat was mostly acquisition accounting. Adjusted EPS was $21.70 against a $9 consensus. Revenue was $14.9B against $13.5B. Cox was consolidated after the Aug 19-20 close.
- GAAP net loss was about $2.1B to $2.4B, from a $6.3B non-cash franchise impairment. It was partly offset by a $1.4B gain on debt extinguishment.
- On a pro forma basis, revenue fell 1.5% to $16.5B and residential revenue fell 4.1%. Adjusted EBITDA fell 4.0% to $6.6B, or 3.0% excluding transition costs.
- Pro forma Internet customers fell by 233k, against 171k a year earlier. Legacy Charter lost 156k (109k a year earlier) and legacy Cox lost 77k. Management blamed weaker connects, not higher churn.
- Mobile added 508k pro forma lines. Video losses narrowed.
- Free cash flow was $674M, against $1.62B a year earlier.
- Buybacks fell to $19M, from $963M in Q1 and $838M in Q2. Cash is going to debt reduction.
- Full-year EBITDA guidance has gone from slight growth to about a 3% pro forma decline. Management gave no timeline for a return to growth.
- The CFO is leaving. Kevin Howard, the chief accounting officer, is interim CFO.

**The plan the rally is pricing**
- Charter is targeting $2B in annualized opex savings over 18 months, with none realized yet. Management says frontline sales and service staff are not targeted.
- Cox synergies are now expected to exceed $1B, up from $800M earlier this year. About half should arrive in the first half of 2027.
- Capex is about $13B in 2026 and at or below $11B in 2027. Management expects significant free cash flow growth as capex falls.
- Leverage is 3.93x against a 3.5x target and should end 2026 below 3.9x.
- Since the Sept 16 "Spectrum Day" launch across Cox markets, Cox Internet losses have roughly halved and its mobile net adds roughly tripled. This is the best early evidence for the bull case.

**Tender offer**
- Charter subsidiaries are offering cash for up to $1.5B of eight series of senior secured notes.
- The notes carry coupons of 3.5% to 4.8%, mature 2041 to 2062, and total $11.6B eligible.
- Pricing is at spreads of 2.05 to 2.5 points over Treasuries, so Charter buys well below par. That is value-accretive debt reduction.
- The offer expires Nov 17, with settlement expected Nov 19.
- It is a small piece of roughly $108B to $109B of debt. The stock reaction is more about sentiment than economics.

**Background**
- Cox closed Aug 19-20 at $34.5B after California approval. Liberty Broadband was folded in at the same time, at 0.236 Charter shares per Liberty Broadband share.
- A Reuters brief dated "Nov 13" about the Liberty Broadband deal appears to be an old item. Treat it as stale.
- The brand is moving to Cox Communications operating under the Spectrum brand.
- Nick Jeffery became COO on Sept 1.
- The stock fell 8.1% on Sept 9 and peaked around $160.70 on Sept 3.

**Street and sector**
- Analyst ratings are split: six Buy, six Hold, six Sell. The mean target is about $176, down slightly.
- Before earnings, Citi had a Buy at $180 (one source says it was raised to $150 from $140, which conflicts). Morgan Stanley cut to $135 from $140 on Nov 5. Wells Fargo has Underweight at $101. Goldman has Sell at $125. StoneX cut to $200 from $380.
- Several targets sit above the price and several below, so the analyst range brackets the current level.
- Bears cite fixed wireless, fiber overbuild, mobile-only switching and aggressive promotions. Management says it has not seen meaningful share loss to Starlink so far.
- New Street expects no cable subscriber growth this decade. TD Cowen expected record sector losses in Q3.
- The legacy Cox business has churn about 10% above Charter's and revenue down 4.5%.
- The value-focused go-to-market approach risks lower revenue per customer. Pro forma residential revenue per customer fell 1.6%.

**What I could not find**
- No news dated Nov 11 to 16 beyond price recaps.
- No short interest data.
- No SEC filing text for the tender.
- No insider or buyback news. Management has said it expects some buybacks, but they are small.

**Read for the 1 to 10 session window**
- **For a long:** The cost plan is credible. Cox early signs are positive. Valuation is depressed. The tender is a small positive. The stock could extend the squeeze-like momentum.
- **Against a long:** The stock is up 28% in 20 days and 14.6% in 5, at 3 ATR above its 20-day average, with RSI 67. It is below a falling 200-day average, so the trend is still down.
- **Against a long:** There is no new catalyst after the tender settles. Broadband losses and the FCF decline are unresolved. Prior rallies here (September) faded.
- **Risks:** A downside gap on any sector headline, such as Comcast, a broadband-loss commentary or an analyst downgrade, would hit a name that has just doubled off its low in relative terms.

agents.report:
**Middleby (MIDD): research as of the evening of Mon 2026-11-16**

**The story**

MIDD is now a pure commercial-foodservice equipment maker, and the stock is rebounding from a post-spin low. Three things happened in 2026:

- **Residential:** a 51% stake in the Residential Kitchen group was sold to 26North for about $540M. About $565M of net proceeds were received in 2026 and used to cut debt and buy back stock.
- **Food Processing spin:** it was spun off as Midera (ticker MFP) on July 6, 2026, one-for-one, and began trading July 7. The old MIDD price history is therefore pre-spin and not comparable with today's.
- **Brewing exit:** the Brewing & Distilling group (Ss Brewtech, Deutsche Beverage + Process, Wild Goose Filling) is being shut down, announced Sept 9. It had about $24M of 2025 sales and a loss of about $9M of adjusted EBITDA. Wind-down should be done by year-end. Management says this adds about 40 bps to 2026 margin, starting Q1 2027.

**Price path**

- **Aug 11 (Q2 report):** sales beat, but the post-spin guidance was read as a margin squeeze. The stock fell, by 3% to 10% depending on the source.
- **Oct 12:** the close was 105.37, near the low.
- **Oct 30:** it closed at 118.95.
- **Nov 5 (Q3 report):** it jumped, about +5.8% premarket and +4.9% on the 6th. Several outlets put the gain at about 14.8% on the week.
- **Mon Nov 9 and Tue Nov 10:** the 20-day high of 141.43 was set Nov 9 or 10, which MarketBeat (dated Nov 10) calls Monday, and the stock crossed above its 200-day average on that high. It has since drifted to about 135-136, so the ~26% gain over 20 days is mostly the earnings gap plus follow-through.
- **Nov 16 (Monday):** your close was 136.09. I found no news on Monday.

Some price series are not spin-adjusted. MarketBeat shows a 200-day of about 137 and a 52-week range of 102-180, while your screen shows 120.95 and 89.16-148.55. Don't compare the two directly.

**Q3 (reported Nov 5) beat on every line**

- **Sales:** a record $652.6M, up 7.7% with all of it organic. This is the third straight quarter of high-single-digit growth.
- **Adjusted EPS:** $2.07 versus roughly $1.75 expected and $1.74 a year ago.
- **Adjusted EBITDA:** $155.8M, a 23.9% margin, above the $143-150M guidance.
- **Guidance:** 2026 raised to adjusted EPS of $7.13-7.29, up from $6.73-6.89. Consensus before the report was about $7.2. Q4 EPS guidance is $1.76-1.92.
- **Longer term:** the 2028 targets were reaffirmed, with a 25-27% EBITDA margin and 10-15% adjusted EPS growth.
- **Demand:** quick-service restaurants (QSR) were strong, with convenience stores strong in beverage, ice and rapid-cook. International grew 14%, about 30% of sales. Dealers were flat against a tough comparison.
- **Free cash flow:** $117M in Q3.
- **Balance sheet:** net debt is $1.64B, net leverage 2.8x. A new $3B five-year credit facility was signed Nov 4.
- **Buybacks:** 1.0M shares ($106M) in Q3 and 4.8M year to date (9.7%). The call put Q4-to-date at $76M, which is a large, ongoing bid. Management said about 11% of shares have been retired this year.
- **CEO succession:** Chief Commercial Officer Steve Spittle succeeds Tim FitzGerald as CEO on April 1, 2027. This is a planned handover.

**Analysts**

- **JPMorgan:** target raised to 165 from 145 on Nov 6-7, Overweight.
- **Canaccord:** target raised to 160 from 152, Buy.
- **Others:**
  - Barclays: 145, Overweight (Aug).
  - RBC: 147 (Sept).
  - KeyCorp: 152 (July).
  - Oppenheimer: 160, Outperform (Aug).
- **Consensus:** six Buy, two Hold, one Sell, with an average target of about 160-162. At 136 that is only about 18% upside, and most targets were raised only to just above the current price.

**Concerns and caveats**

- **Q4 slowdown:** Q4 organic growth is guided to about 4.4%, against 7.7% in Q3 and about 7.5% for the year. Analysts questioned the deceleration.
- **Cost pressure:** management flagged $10-15M of extra second-half inflation, a beverage investment that costs about 100 bps of margin, and geopolitical cost pressure with weak Asia and Middle East conditions. A $5M tariff refund helped Q3, and almost none is expected in Q4.
- **Restaurant exposure:** there is concentration in big QSR chains and some exposure to restaurant traffic.
- **GAAP is messy:** Q3 GAAP EPS from continuing operations was $0.43, and the total was $(0.04) after the discontinued operations. The adjusted-versus-GAAP gap is wide, and the high trailing P/E in the aggregators is distorted by it.
- **Short interest:** about 3.6% of float in August, from a third-party source, so low.
- **Insiders:** I found no insider trades.

**Upcoming events**

- No earnings until Q4, which Middleby has historically reported in late February. I did not confirm the date.
- No other scheduled catalysts found. Watch the brewing wind-down completing at year-end, and any further buyback disclosure.

**Read for the 1-10 session window**

- The fundamental story is clean: a beat, a raise, buybacks, and a simpler company. The rally is a post-earnings re-rating from a depressed post-spin base.
- Entry here is stretched, with RSI 78, no catalyst for days, and volume down to 0.7x normal. Nothing I found points to a fundamental reason for a near-term fall either.
- The risk to a long is a pullback to fill the gap, around 127-130, rather than bad news. The 20-day high of 141.43 is the first resistance, then 148.55.

agents.report:
**FIS research for the 1-10 session window (as of 12:35 AM CT, Tue 2026-11-17)**

I found no fresh negative news explaining Monday's -4.2%. It looks like continued selling after the November 4 reset, plus a possible tax-loss or capitulation flavor. New searches stopped producing anything new after the Q3 release, the Q2 history, analyst moves, insider buys, legal notices and the sector context. I could not open several pages (Yahoo call transcript, GuruFocus call highlights, Trader's Union, GF value pages), so the call-level color comes from secondary summaries.

**The story**
- **The deal behind the debt.** FIS bought Issuer Solutions (now "Total Issuing Solutions") on Jan 9, 2026. It sold its 45% Worldpay stake the same day for a $2.2B gain. The Issuer deal cost about $7.9B net of cash, funded with about $7.7B of term loans, which were later replaced by senior notes on Mar 10. Debt is now $20.8B, and goodwill rose to $25.0B from $17.8B ([Q3 10-Q](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001136893/000113689326000063/fis-20260930.htm)).
- **Interest cost.** Net interest expense roughly doubled year on year, from $90M to $199M in Q3 ([BriefGlance](https://briefglance.com/articles/fis-cfo-exits-as-challenging-2027-outlook-triggers-24-stock-plunge)).
- **Serial guidance cuts.** The Aug 4 Q2 report cut pro forma revenue guidance and the stock fell about 9.5% ([Seeking Alpha](https://seekingalpha.com/news/4624539-fidelity-national-information-stock-slumps-after-cutting-guidance-mixed-q2-results)). Analyst downgrades followed in September (UBS, Wells Fargo, Deutsche Bank target cut), with new lows near $34 ([Investing.com](https://www.investing.com/news/company-news/fidelity-national-information-services-stock-hits-52week-low-at-3415-93CH-4922881)). The stock was already down about 41% year to date before Nov 4.
- **Nov 4 (Q3) was the break.** The stock fell about 24%, its worst day since Nov 2022, and landed at its lowest since 2012 ([Bloomberg Law](https://news.bloomberglaw.com/mergers-and-acquisitions/fis-plunges-as-fintech-halts-buybacks-some-m-a-to-deleverage), [Jax Daily Record](https://www.jaxdailyrecord.com/news/2026/nov/12/fis-stock-drops-after-earnings-report/)). Four things landed together:
  - FY26 adjusted EPS guidance was cut to $5.82-5.89 from $6.15-6.24.
  - Preliminary 2027 guidance has adjusted EPS down high-single to low-double digits, margins flat to down 100 bps, and a return to normal growth only in 2028.
  - CFO Kehoe left effective Nov 5. Chief accounting officer Alexandra Brooks is interim CFO and the board is searching.
  - Buybacks are curtailed and tuck-in M&A is paused until gross leverage reaches about 2.8x.
- **Official numbers.** Q3 adjusted EPS was $1.61 (+6.6%), pro forma revenue +3.7%, pro forma EBITDA +5.2%, and Q3 free cash flow $862M excluding transaction taxes. The FCF target of $2.15-2.25B was kept ([8-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001136893/000113689326000061/q32026ex991.htm)).
- **Why revenue slipped.** Banking pro forma growth guidance fell to 3.5-4% from 5-5.5%. Large clients pushed back conversion dates, with fewer than 10 clients affected and some now scheduled as late as Q3 2027. Bank consolidation also shifted revenue timing. Customers are moving from on-premises licenses to cloud subscriptions, which cuts near-term license revenue. SNAP-participant pressure is expected into 1H27 ([PYMNTS](https://www.pymnts.com/earnings/2026/fis-cuts-banking-growth-outlook-amid-project-delays/)). Management also cited higher cyber and technology investment.
- **Aftermath.** The stock fell 5 straight sessions, down 29.4% from the pre-report level, to a $28.34 close on Nov 9 while the S&P was flat ([Trefis](https://www.trefis.com/stock/fis/articles/623921/a-5-day-losing-streak-has-fidelity-national-information-services-stock-down-29/2026-11-10)). Later reports have a bounce of about 6.7% to about $30.21 (GuruFocus headline), then the Nov 16 close of $28.30. I did not pin down what drove either move.

**Analysts, insiders, legal**
- Six downgrades followed Nov 4. Named ones: J.P. Morgan to neutral (target $53 to $38), Oppenheimer to Perform, William Blair to Market Perform ("FIS could be an attractive takeover candidate"), Bank of America to neutral ($33), UBS target $32, Barclays $30 equal weight. The MarketBeat consensus is Hold, with an average target of about $42 ([Cerbat Gem](https://www.thecerbatgem.com/2026/11/06/fidelity-national-information-services-nysefis-reaches-new-52-week-low-following-analyst-downgrade.html)).
- Director Kourtney Gibson bought 1,800 shares at $29.00 on Nov 6 (about $52K). Chairman Goldstein bought 1,585 shares at $36.40 on Oct 15, in lieu of his cash retainer. Both are small. Other November Form 4s are tax withholding on vesting, not open-market buys ([SEC Form 4](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001136893/000162828026072763/wk-form4_1794345685.xml)).
- Plaintiff firms (Levi & Korsinsky, SueWallSt, Bronstein Gewirtz) have posted "investigation" notices from Nov 4 to 15 ([PR Newswire](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/fis-investigation-notice-levi--korsinsky-notifies-investors-of-pending-investigation-into-fidelity-national-information-services-fis-302929829.html)). These are solicitations, with no filed complaint and no SEC action that I found. They tend to add noise and nothing more.
- An older Merchant Solutions securities case was settled and got final approval on Jul 9, 2026.

**Valuation and balance sheet**
- Forward P/E is about 4-6x depending on the source, and GuruFocus's GF Value is far above price (low reliability). GuruFocus flags it as a possible value trap, with financial strength 3/10 ([GuruFocus](https://www.gurufocus.com/news/9203104/is-fidelity-national-information-services-inc-fis-a-bargain-after-42-drop-gf-value-says-undervalued)).
- Market cap is about $14.6B on 515M shares, against $20.8B of debt.
- The dividend is $0.44 quarterly ($1.76 a year), a yield of about 6% at $28.4, and the sources I saw disagree on yield and were stale. Management plans per-share dividend growth in line with adjusted EPS growth. The record date is Dec 14 and the payment date Dec 28 ([FIS release](https://www.fisglobal.com/about-us/media-room/press-release/2026/fis-announces-quarterly-dividend-october-29)). That is outside a 1-10 session window if it counts as the ex-date (the Dec 14 date is my inference).
- A $378M Worldpay CVR liability is due Oct 12, 2027.
- Sector context: core-processing peers are also depressed. Fiserv crashed in Oct 2025 and is down about 64% over 12 months; FIS is down about 45% over 12 months (as of late September) ([DK Street Journal](https://www.dkstreetjournal.com/a-2026-09-27-77a558dc)). This is company-specific plus sector sentiment, which fits the screen's finding of no correlation with sector funds or the S&P.

**Read for the one-to-ten-session trade**
- The bear case is credible: three guidance cuts in four months, falling 2027 EPS, interest costs doubling, no buybacks, an interim CFO and a downgrade wave. This is a fundamental reset, not a one-day overreaction.
- The bounce case rests on how cheap it is, the buyback and tuck-in pause being a known quantity, the small director buy, the possible takeover talk (one analyst's remark), and a price sitting on the 52-week low of $27.93 (about 1.3% below the last price).

- A break below $27.93 with no support nearby is the main risk. With ATR at 6% of price, stops need to be wide.

agents.report:
**OGS (ONE Gas) research, written 12:35 AM CT Tue 2026-11-17**

**Bottom line:** This is a stable regulated gas utility that has had a good fundamental quarter, and the stock is up about 5% in two weeks. I found no company-specific news explaining Monday's level. The setup looks like a sector and rate-driven drift higher, not a catalyst. The main known catalyst, the early-December 2027 guidance, is likely at least two to three weeks away and probably outside a 1 to 10 session window. I found no ex-dividend effect left to come, and no scheduled company event inside the window.

**Business**
- ONE Gas is a pure-play natural gas distributor serving Oklahoma (Oklahoma Natural Gas), Kansas (Kansas Gas Service) and Texas (Texas Gas Service). It has about 716K Texas and 649K Kansas customers.
- Earnings come from rate-regulated infrastructure spending. 2026 capex is about $800M, and net property, plant and equipment rose to $7.47B from $7.12B at year-end.
- Management targets 3 to 4% long-term annual EPS growth.

**Q3 results (released Nov 2)**
- Adjusted EPS was $0.53 against about $0.48 expected and $0.47 a year ago. Revenue was $391M, up 3.2% but about 2.5% below consensus.
- Operating and maintenance expense was flat at $137.1M after rising 8.6% in Q1 and 6.6% in Q2.
- This is the second guidance raise this year. 2026 adjusted EPS guidance is now $4.95 to $5.01 (midpoint $4.98), and the range sits entirely above the original $4.83 to $4.95.
- Weather was very warm: Q3 was 97% warmer than normal and the nine months 23% warmer. Weather-normalization mechanisms cushioned the effect on operating income.
- The dividend is $0.68 a quarter ($2.72 a year), roughly a 3.2% yield at $84. The record date was Nov 16 and it is payable Dec 3. I did not confirm the ex-date, so check whether it fell on Monday, since that would explain a flat day.

**Regulatory**
- Texas: a $36.9M Gas Reliability Infrastructure Program (GRIP) increase took effect in July.
- Kansas: a $14.3M Gas System Reliability Surcharge (GSRS) increase was approved Sept 22 and took effect in October.
- Oklahoma: a $28.7M performance-based rate increase was approved Oct 14, with interim rates in effect since June 26.
- The Oklahoma order has been appealed to the Oklahoma Supreme Court. The release gives no timeline or possible outcome, so this is the main unresolved legal item.
- Oklahoma Corporation Commission turnover adds uncertainty to the general rate case, which the company expects to file in 2027.

**Growth angle**
- Four contracted large-load projects (data centers, a Texas LNG-related project) add about $22M of annual revenue and $200M of capital. One Oklahoma data-center line is due to start service in November.
- Eight late-stage opportunities represent about 3 GW and up to 1 BCF/day, with about 20 more in early evaluation. The largest, Western Farmers, is due in service in Q3 2028. Management would not size the company's own capital share.

**Negatives**
- Management said 2027 EPS growth will be below trend, mainly because the performance-based mechanism ends and the Oklahoma general rate case process is longer. Full 2027 guidance and the long-term plan come in early December.
- Commercial-paper exposure is unhedged. A 100 basis point move in Fed funds is worth about $0.09 of EPS. One source says the Fed hiked in September and signaled another increase, but I could not confirm that independently.
- The company issued $375M of 10-year notes at 5.45% in August.
- Equity is covered by forward sales at about $82 a share, which is near the current price. That is a possible supply overhang, but it is sold forward and cleared for 2026.
- Equity needs through 2030 are unchanged.

**Analysts**
- Consensus is "Moderate Buy" (7 buy, 6 hold), with an average target of about $87.
- Early November target changes: BTIG to $95 (Buy), Scotiabank to $87 (Outperform), Wells Fargo to $86 (Equal Weight), Mizuho raised, and Morgan Stanley to $86 (Equal Weight, undated).
- At $84 the stock is within about 3% of the average target, so there is little consensus upside.

**Price context**
- A Nov 3 article put the stock near $79.94, below its 200-day average, saying it had "gone essentially nowhere" through two guidance raises. It then moved to about $82.22 by Nov 11 and $84.00 on Monday.
- Rising Treasury yields hurt utilities on Nov 10, so the move higher likely tracks a sector bounce or yields easing. I could not verify what yields or the sector did on Nov 12 to 16.
- One search gave a 52-week high of $90.78 set on 04/09/26, against 89.27 in your screen. That is a small data discrepancy worth knowing about, and either way the stock is well below the high.

**What I could not find**
- No OGS-specific headline from Nov 12 to 16.
- No dated price or yield tape for last week.
- No Oklahoma Supreme Court schedule.
- No exact 2027 guidance date, only "early December" (last year's release was around Dec 1).

**Read for a 1 to 10 session trade:** There is no company catalyst inside the window. The stock is stretched (RSI 76) on sector and yield moves, which makes it exposed to a yield backup. Upside has a fundamental floor from the guidance raises, but it is capped by the $82 equity-placement price and the consensus target around $87. The December guidance event could be a mild negative given the below-trend 2027 warning, and a lean on it would be short-dated.

agents.report:
**OPCH is no longer trading on fundamentals or technicals. It is a pending all-cash takeout at $32.05 per share, and Monday's 31.71 close sits 1.07% below that price. I'd skip it, because the realistic gain over 1–10 sessions is a few cents.**

**What happened**
- **Guidance cut, April 30, 2026.** After Q1, OPCH cut 2026 revenue guidance to about $5.68–5.78B, against consensus near $5.94B. Q1 revenue was about $1.35B versus roughly $1.40B expected. The stock fell about 24–30%, to roughly $19–20.
  - Third-party explanations point to drug pricing, faster conversion to cheaper biosimilars, and a weaker chronic-therapy mix. I did not see these confirmed by the company.
  - TD Cowen cut its target from $37 to $23 and Bank of America moved to Neutral. Law firms then solicited shareholders for investigations.
- **Buyout interest, May 2026.**
  - Per the proxy, CD&R had been in touch since early 2025. Four other sponsors, called Parties A–D, each signed a confidentiality agreement and then dropped out without a proposal.
  - Management also spoke with Parties E, F and G and an unnamed strategic party in January 2026. Nothing came of it.
  - On May 18–19, CD&R and McKesson sent a non-binding indication of $28–32 per share.
- **Deal announced October 6, 2026.**
  - The price is $32.05 cash, an enterprise value of about $5.8B. That is about 37% over the October 5 close and about 42% over the $22.64 close on October 2.
  - CD&R would own about 51% and McKesson about 49%, with McKesson investing about $1.4B.
  - The board backed it unanimously. The stock jumped about 33% to roughly $31.
- **Q3 results, November 4.**
  - Revenue was $1,493.5M (+4.1%), GAAP EPS $0.38 and adjusted EPS $0.49. Adjusted EBITDA was $124.6M.
  - There was no earnings call and the company withdrew its guidance.

**Deal mechanics, from the merger proxy**
- **Shareholder vote:** December 15, 2026 at 9 AM CT, virtual. Record date was November 3, with 149.8M shares outstanding. Approval needs a majority of all outstanding shares.
- **Antitrust:** The Hart-Scott-Rodino (HSR) filing went in November 3, with early termination requested. The 30-day waiting period expires December 3 unless it is ended early or the FTC or DOJ issues a Second Request. I found no news on either outcome.
- **State approvals:** Indiana, Massachusetts and Washington filings are needed before closing. Other state healthcare and pharmacy approvals are closing conditions.
- **Closing:** Guided to the first half of 2027. The outside date is October 5, 2027.
- **Financing and fees:** No financing condition. Committed funding is $3.15B of debt plus a $500M revolver and about $2.87B of equity, backed by CD&R Fund XII and McKesson guarantees. The company owes a $146M break fee and the buyers owe $292M.
- **Topping bids:** It is a no-shop with a fiduciary exception, not a go-shop. No rival bid has surfaced, and the earlier suitors had dropped out.
- **Litigation:** The proxy lists no suits challenging the deal, only one books-and-records or disclosure demand. The Levi & Korsinsky notice concerns the 2026 guidance, not the sale price.

**What this means for a 1–10 session trade**
- **Spread:** 0.34, or 1.07% gross, for a close in roughly 3–7 months. That is a thin spread, so the market sees a high chance of completion. It may also leave a little room for a bump.
- **After-hours:** The 31.71 print is consistent with an arbitrage-pinned stock. The 0.21x range compression and the 0.8x volume fit that too.
- **Screen signals:** The 75 RSI, the move above the 50-day average, the 20-day-high breakout and the 52-week high of 36.80 are all misleading here. The high is from before the April collapse, and the stock cannot trade up through the offer without a new bid. Momentum and mean-reversion signals carry no information.
- **Catalysts in the window:** Possible HSR news before December 3 and the proxy mailing. A Second Request would likely widen the spread, and early termination would narrow it by a few cents.
- **Downside tail:** Deal-break risk with a standalone value near $19–23 is small but large in size.
- **Upside tail:** A topping bid is unlikely given no rival interest.
- **Analyst targets:** The snapshots I found ranged $29–39 and were stale or undated. They don't matter for a deal-pinned stock.

**Limits of the search**
- I couldn't open the proxy's later sections, so I did not see the price negotiation from $28–32 up to $32.05, the board's reasons, the fairness opinion or any shareholder opposition.
- I did not confirm any news after November 10, such as an HSR outcome.
- Chartmill and some other pages returned 403 errors. The search tool's summaries made one error: it described the stock as already trading near the deal price and misdated the guidance cut to May.

agents.report:
**BABA research, as of 12:35 AM CT Tue 2026-11-17**

**Bottom line:** BABA's slide is mostly a policy and sentiment shock about chip access, not a change in the business. It has run into a binary earnings event three sessions away. The most important fact for Tuesday is that Hong Kong already traded after the US close, and Alibaba's Hong Kong shares were down about 5%. Your 90.92 after-hours print likely understates the gap-down risk at Tuesday's US open.

**What happened**

1. **Aug 20 and Aug 23-26, the backdrop.**
   - June-quarter adjusted EPS was RMB 8.52 per ADS against RMB 10.53 consensus. That is a miss, and TIKR counts five straight misses.
   - Cloud revenue grew 45% to RMB 48.4B. Capex rose 75% to RMB 67.7B. Free cash flow was an outflow of RMB 44.7B.
   - Customer management revenue fell 7%. Quick commerce revenue grew 45%. The AI Labs and Applications unit lost RMB 13.9B.
   - Alibaba then placed 710M new shares in Hong Kong at HK$112.70, about 3.7% of its share count. That raised about US$10.2B, mostly for compute. It was the largest placement in Hong Kong and its first since 2019, and the stock fell as much as 10% that day.
   - Insiders were mixed: the chairman and CEO bought about $15M combined, and the CFO sold about $1.4M.
2. **Nov 9-12, the Nvidia and Megaspeed scandal.**
   - Reports linked Singapore-based Megaspeed to Jensen Huang's personal scandal. WSJ says it brokered nearly $12B of Nvidia chip orders for China.
   - Alibaba is reportedly Megaspeed's anchor and largest client. The FT reports Alibaba's Singapore unit lent money to Megaspeed's Malaysian arm.
   - Short seller Culper Research (which is short Nvidia) says that unit carried $4.1B in prepayments. No filing shows those reached Megaspeed.
   - Alibaba's role is reported, not proven. The US probe targets Megaspeed, not Alibaba, and Megaspeed denies diverting chips.
   - Sources say Huang resigned as Nvidia CEO on Nov 12. I could not confirm that from a primary source.
3. **Nov 12, the first drop.** The Information reported Commerce was finalizing a rule on remote access to chips. BABA fell about 8% to about 93.4, and Hong Kong shares closed about 6.8% lower.
4. **Mon Nov 16, the rule became real.**
   - The Bureau of Industry and Security (the Commerce unit that controls chip exports) issued an interim final rule, "Addressing Remote Access to Advanced Semiconductors".
   - It requires licenses for advanced chips going to data centers that give significant compute (above a 12M TPP threshold) to companies headquartered in China or Macau. This applies anywhere in the world.
   - It adds license requirements for chip shipments to Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia and Brazil.
   - Data centers already serving Chinese firms have 90 days after the effective date to get a license. The posted document leaves the effective date blank.
   - There is a narrow exception for recommender systems only. Generative AI is excluded from it.
   - A separate Remote Access Security Act has passed the House and awaits the Senate.
5. **Mon Nov 16, the same day.**
   - Alibaba launched its Qwen4-Max flagship model, claiming a 60% lower task cost. This had no visible price support.
   - Baidu's Q3 results came out: revenue fell 1% (sixth straight decline), adjusted EPS missed, AI cloud rose 94%, and online marketing fell 22%.
6. **Tue Nov 17, Hong Kong session, after the US close.**
   - Alibaba fell nearly 5%, Baidu nearly 7%, Tencent more than 3%, and JD 2.6%.
   - The Hang Seng fell 0.8%.
   - China's domestic semiconductor index rose nearly 6%. The market is reading the rule as a win for local chips, a loss for the platforms that rent offshore Nvidia capacity.

**Earnings setup (Thu Nov 19, before the US open, 7:00 AM ET call)**
- Alibaba's own notice confirms the date. Some sites list Nov 18, 23 or 24, and those are wrong.
- Cloud revenue consensus is up 50-55%. Citi has RMB 60.5B and a 12.5% margin, Morgan Stanley 55% growth and a 13.5% margin, BofA 52%.
- BofA expects group adjusted EBITA of RMB 30B against a consensus of RMB 26B. It sees AI-lab losses narrowing to about RMB 11B. Jefferies sees quick-commerce losses narrowing to about RMB 9.8B.
- Consensus adjusted EPS is about RMB 11 per ADS. The bar for ending the five-miss streak is a big rebound in profit.
- Bloomberg-compiled options imply a 5.7% move. OptionsLam shows 8.2% weekly. Alibaba beat the implied move in five of the last eight reports.
- Analyst targets cluster at $160-200, with a consensus of about $184-191. They are stale and mostly pre-date the rule.
- Forward P/E is about 12x, against 25x in January.

**Reading it for a 1-10 session trade**
- **The market expects strong cloud numbers.** The risk is guidance. A beat on cloud with vague compute supply could still sell off. Management said "AI and Cloud growth will accelerate further". The rule now questions how that compute gets supplied.
- **Why the stock could bounce.** It is oversold and cheap. It is exposed to scandal sentiment more than to fundamentals. Chinese regulators have stepped in before when these stocks sold off. T-Head chip supply, which is not covered by the rule, is the likely counterargument on the call.
- **Why it might not.**
  - The rule is law, not a rumor, and it is still unfolding. Analysts have not yet cut numbers.
  - A "no turn yet" chart with a falling 50-day below the 200-day, and Hong Kong down another 5%, suggests an opening gap below 90.
  - The stock has missed earnings five times running.
  - Free cash flow is negative and the share count just rose.
- **Gap risk.** A stop near the old low (91.99) is likely to trigger at the open on the Hong Kong lead alone. If you want to wait for the earnings reaction, the entry has to be sized for roughly a 6-10% move either way on Thursday.

**What I could not find**
- Alibaba's own response to the rule. The earnings call is the likely venue.
- A Monday close or US pre-market for Tuesday. The 5% Hong Kong drop is the best proxy for the US open.
- How much of Alibaba's cloud capacity is actually overseas. Analysts say this is the key question for Nov 19.
- Anything on the securities class action that TIKR mentions. I found no sourcing for it.
