**OGS research brief, as of 12:55 AM CT Tue 2026-11-17**

**Bottom line:** OGS is rising on a real fundamental catalyst. It beat Q3 and raised guidance for the second time this year. Management has also promised a December five-year plan refresh that analysts expect to be positive. The weak points are a known below-trend 2027, an Oklahoma rate-case wrinkle, rising rate and fuel costs, and an entry price of 84 (RSI 76) after a 12.6% run in 20 days. Monday was also the ex-dividend date, so the move up is not distorted by a pending $0.68 payout. I found no rumors, M&A or one-off news driving it.

**The story**
- **Q3 report (Nov 2, call Nov 3):**
  - Adjusted EPS was $0.53 versus $0.47 a year earlier and about $0.48 expected.
  - 2026 adjusted EPS guidance rose to $4.95 to $5.01 (midpoint $4.98) from $4.89 to $4.95. It was raised once earlier this year, from $4.83 to $4.95.
  - New rates added $13.5M to operating income in Q3 and $57.2M year to date.
  - Q3 O&M (operations and maintenance cost) was flat year over year, after a 7.5% rise in the first half.
  - Q3 weather was far warmer than normal and the year to date is 23% warmer, but weather-normalization mechanisms absorbed most of it.
  - Per BTIG, the stock beat utilities by about 2 points on the report day.
- **Texas House Bill 4384:** It is now worth about $0.45 of 2026 EPS, up from the original $0.35 estimate.
- **Kansas:** A surcharge of about $14.3M was approved Sept 22 and took effect in October (about $7M last year). Texas GRIP (infrastructure program) rates of $36.9M took effect in July.
- **Large-load (data center, generation and LNG) pipeline:**
  - Four projects add about $22M of annual revenue and about $200M of capital. Two are due in service in Q4 2026.
  - A company-funded Texas LNG project is due in Q1 2027.
  - Eight late-stage projects total about 3 GW of generation and up to 1 Bcf/day of demand, plus 20 early-stage ones. The larger ones contribute in 2028 to 2030.
  - Management declined to quantify the company-funded capital until December.
- **Financing:**
  - Capex is about $800M a year (about $4.3B over five years).
  - The 2026 financing is complete: $375M of 5.45% 10-year notes in August, with no new equity needed in 2026.
  - Forward equity sales are priced around $82 a share, which sits close to the current price.
  - The next debt maturity is Q2 2029.
- **Dividend:** $0.68 a quarter, unchanged. Record date Nov 16, payable Dec 3.

**Upcoming catalyst:** The five-year plan refresh is due in December, which falls inside or just past your 1 to 10 session window. I could not find the date, and the company's release does not give one. It will include a new growth rate (the current target is 5% to 7% EPS growth through 2030), large-load capital and a 2030 outlook. On the call, a question put 2030 EPS at around $6. BTIG and others are positioning for upside to consensus. That makes a run-up plausible, but it is also a "buy the rumor" setup.

**Risks and negatives**
- **2027 is guided below trend:** Oklahoma has no performance-based rate mechanism and general rate case timing is mechanical. Management also cited higher Fed rates and fuel prices as headwinds. A 100 bp change in Fed funds moves EPS by about $0.09. The 2030 outcome depends partly on rates easing.
- **Oklahoma:**
  - The Oklahoma Corporation Commission approved the performance-based rate case on Oct 14 ($28.7M), and the order has been appealed to the Oklahoma Supreme Court.
  - Two state legislators (Gann and West) are challenging Oklahoma Natural Gas matters, including a $29M increase, a $98M increase, storm bonds and fuel costs, over lack of audits and customer intervention. They are partisan sources.
  - I found no Supreme Court ruling, but a decision on the 2023 fuel cost appeal could come at any time.
  - The CFO said the next Oklahoma general rate case may seek a higher cost of capital. Commission turnover after the election was described as no concern.
- **Earnings quality:** Adjusted EPS includes a deferred carrying cost ($12.2M year to date versus $3.4M last year) that GAAP excludes. GAAP EPS was $0.49 in Q3.
- **Cost pressures:** Employee, outside service and bad debt costs are up.
- **Where the stock sits:** The 12.6% 20-day gain follows the post-earnings run, and the RSI is 76. The sell-side average target is about $87 (13 analysts, 7 Buy and 6 Hold), so there is only about 4% to the average target. Targets:

  - Mizuho $90
  - Scotiabank $87 (Outperform)
  - Wells Fargo $86 (Equal Weight)
  - Morgan Stanley $78 (Equal Weight, Oct 21)
  The stock is already above Wells Fargo's and Scotiabank's targets.

**Sector context:** Gas utilities were strong into mid-November. Atmos, Spire and Southwest Gas were up roughly 7% to 13% over a month as of Nov 9. On Nov 9 the utilities sector rose 1.53%, trailing the S&P 500. December natural gas hit $3.34, its highest settlement since June, on cold weather. I found no source linking gas utilities to Treasury yields this month.

**Discrepancies to be aware of**
- Search snippets put the 52-week high at $90.78 (Apr 8, 2026), not your 89.27. That may be a different adjustment or intraday versus close. Either way, the high sits within about 6% to 8% of the current price.

- I could not open the Benzinga transcript (403 error), so the call details come from a GuruFocus and Yahoo summary of the call.

**Read for a 1 to 10 session trade:** The thesis is a catalyst-backed uptrend with a December event ahead. The offsets are an extended chart (RSI 76, 2.5 ATR above its 20-day average), valuation near analyst targets, and 2027 caveats that management has already disclosed. The 50-day is still below the 200-day, but price is above both. A pullback toward 80 to 82 (the forward-equity price area) would be a better entry than chasing at 84.

**Cboe Global Markets (CBOE): research for the 1–10 session decision, as of 12:55 AM CT Tuesday 2026-11-17**

**Summary:** The fundamental story is strong and a lot of it is already priced in. Shares are up from about $266 on Sept 29 to $377, roughly +42% in seven weeks. That is a re-rating on a de-risked franchise and an earnings beat-and-raise. The next hard company catalysts are the KPI-contract launch and the Dec 6–7 start of 23/5 equities trading. Nothing in the evidence explains a turn within 1–10 sessions. Several details also cut against the bull case.

**Setup and the climb**
- Sept 29: Cboe and S&P Dow Jones Indices extended the exclusive SPX/VIX license through 2051. The prior term ran to 2032–33. The stock jumped as much as 10% that day, to about $266.
- Oct 22: the board added $550M to the buyback, for about $1.0B of capacity.
- Oct 23: Morgan Stanley's Michael Cyprys reiterated Buy and raised his target from $358 to $450, with the stock at $335.53.
- Oct 30: Q3 results, described below. Shares rose about 6–7%.
- Nov 3: shares fell 0.9% to $346.06 on news that Cboe had joined the lawsuit against the CFTC.
- Nov 11–12: new highs at $371.21 on Nov 11 and $373 on Nov 12.
- Monday's close was $377.50. The Nov 11 article put the 50-day at $300.77 and the 200-day at $294.66.

**Q3 results (Oct 30)**
- Net revenue was $712.2M, up 18%. Adjusted EPS was $3.63 (up 36%) against about $3.42–3.43 expected. GAAP EPS was $4.08, helped by a $71.5M gain on the Cboe Australia sale.
- Adjusted operating expenses fell 3%, to $204M. Adjusted operating margin was 71.4%.
- Options net revenue was $469.5M, up 23%. Index options average daily volume (ADV) rose 24%, and 0DTE (zero-days-to-expiry) options hit a record 65% of SPX volume. Retail was about 58% of SPX 0DTE.
- Data Vantage (market data) revenue was a record $179.1M, up 13%.
- 2026 guidance was raised: organic net revenue growth to "high teens" from "mid to high teens", and Data Vantage growth to "mid teens" from "low teens". Adjusted operating expenses guidance was lowered to $830–845M.
- Cost savings: the strategic realignment is expected to cut the workforce by about 20%. Savings are $20–25M in 2026 and a $40–50M annualized run rate.
- Management plans to give 2027 expense guidance in early February. Our calendar's Feb 5 earnings date fits that timing.

**Volumes**
- October index options ADV was a record 6.9M contracts, up 25% year on year. SPX ADV was a record 5.5M and SPX 0DTE ADV a record 3.6M.
- Oct 16 and Oct 30 were the two busiest days ever for proprietary index options, at 10.4M and 10.2M contracts.
- Global Trading Hours (the overnight session) set a record at 284K contracts.
- Not everything was up. Multi-listed options ADV fell 10.3% year on year, futures fell 8.3%, and on-exchange U.S. equities fell 24%.
- Q3 options market share slipped to 30.5% from 30.9%. U.S. equity exchange share fell to 8.9% from 9.8%.
- VIX options ADV grew only 3% in Q3. Management said volatility picked up in early Q4 and VIX call volume hit a two-year daily high in October. A calm market would hurt futures and VIX revenue.

**Catalysts and pending items**
- **KPI binary options:** The SEC approved contracts on 23 companies. Cboe Clear U.S. has temporary SEC clearing registration. Robinhood and Interactive Brokers are supporting access, and fees are waived through 2026. Launch was targeted for October and then November, and I found no confirmed date or launch report. On the call, management flagged the launch timing and the regulatory uncertainty over whether event contracts are securities or futures.
- **23/5 U.S. equities on EDGX:** The effective date is Dec 6–7. It depends on industry readiness.
- **Dividend:** $0.86 per share, ex-date Nov 30, a yield of about 0.9%.
- **Notes repayment:** $650M of notes mature in Q1 2027 and will be repaid from cash.
- **Cboe Canada:** The sale to TMX is still pending as of the Q3 call, with a closing timeline unclear.

**Risks and cons**
- **S&P royalty step-up in 2027:** Management calls it de minimis for 2027 growth, but it has not disclosed the fee schedule or a dollar figure. Later adjustments are said to be smaller. SPX fees have not been meaningfully adjusted in several years, and management plans to offset the step-up with pricing optimization and volume.
- **CFTC perpetuals lawsuit:** On Nov 3, Cboe joined a Capital Markets Alliance suit (with Citadel Securities and Healthy Markets) against the CFTC's approval of single-stock perpetual futures. The CFTC has pushed back publicly, and CME is reported to be suing separately. The suit looks defensive, and I found no ruling.
- **Cost pressure:** The Consolidated Audit Trail (CAT) reserve added $14M, and AI-driven hardware and software costs are expected to persist.
- **Volume dependence:** Record 0DTE and retail activity is cyclical. The Pattern Day Trader rule repeal helped XSP (mini-SPX) volume more than double.
- **Valuation:** The stock now sits above the MarketBeat consensus average target of about $363. Consensus was 5 Buy, 8 Hold and 1 Sell as of Nov 11. Trailing P/E is about 190, which is distorted by one-time items. Analysts expected about $6.41 of EPS for the current fiscal year, so the stock trades at roughly 59x that figure. That multiple is unusually high for an exchange and implies large 2027 growth expectations.

**Analyst views (all pre-Nov 12 unless noted)**

I relied on the figures that Cboe's own release and the earnings-call summary agree on. The call summary was cut off at 100,000 of 103,995 characters. **MSI research summary, as of 12:55 AM CT, Tue 2026-11-17**

**The story in one line:** MSI is an earnings-driven re-rating. The Q3 report on Nov 4 beat estimates and raised guidance for the third time this year. The stock then gapped up and has drifted to the Nov 5 high of 548.29. Nothing since then looks like a new catalyst, and no further earnings catalyst falls in a 1–10 session window.

**What happened (primary sources)**
- **Q3 results (Nov 4, after the close, from the 8-K):**
  - Sales were $3,376M, up 12% (organic +5%).
  - Non-GAAP EPS was $4.69, up 16%, against about $4.42 expected.
  - Non-GAAP operating margin was 32.5%, up 200 bps.
  - Orders rose more than 20%.
  - Backlog is a record $16.6B, up 14%.
  - GAAP EPS fell to $3.06. A $0.52 noncash charge for a higher Silvus earnout provision caused that, and it is not an operating problem.
- **Guidance:**
  - FY26 revenue is about $13.05B (was $12.975B).
  - FY26 non-GAAP EPS is $17.94–17.99 (was $17.62–17.72).
  - Operating cash flow is $3.05B.
  - Q4 revenue growth is about 13%, with EPS of $5.47–5.52.
  - Management gave a preliminary 2027 revenue figure of about $14.25B, with formal guidance in February.
- **Reaction:** The stock rose about 4% on Nov 5, from about 497 to 517 per MarketBeat, with an intraday high of 548.29. It then rose from 517 into the 530s, and the CEO's sale on Nov 12 printed at 533.53.
- **Price discrepancy:** One aggregator said the Nov 16 close was 540.58. A MarketBeat piece had Monday trading near 534.41 midday, which fits your 534.17 close, so I treat 540.58 as wrong.

**Growth drivers**
- **Land mobile radio (LMR):**
  - Product orders rose about 25%.
  - A multiyear P25 refresh cycle is early, across more than 1,300 networks.
  - Awards included a $140M Federal Bureau of Prisons order and a $139M, 10-year Louisiana contract.
- **Video and software:** Video grew double digits, and Command Center is expected to grow about 15%. AI Assist is built into the workflows, and nearly all customers pick the premium tier.
- **Silvus (drone and defense radios, bought for $4.4B in 2025):**
  - It is on track for slightly more than $900M of revenue in 2026, with about $300M in Q3.
  - Management guided to about 30% growth in 2027.
  - Capacity has doubled and lead times fell to 12–14 weeks.
  - Management flagged that Silvus revenue is lumpy, and analysts asked about a Q4/Q1 step-down.
- **D-Fend (counter-drone, $1.5B headline, $1.3B net of cash):** It closed in August. Management expects about $185M of revenue on a calendar-year basis, growing 40–50% in 2027.
- **Other deals:** DeepNeuronic ($29M), Exacom ($67M) and Hyper ($23M) are small. The Bell Canada LMR services deal (C$675M) now closes in Q1 or Q2 2027, later than the Q4 2026 date first given.
- **Funding backdrop:** State and local budgets are the majority of the business. Management says DHS is funded through 2029 and is relatively indifferent to the midterms. The counter-drone and defense theme is real, though the search found nothing MSI-specific in the Pentagon drone-spending headlines.

**Concerns**
- **Valuation:**
  - Trailing P/E is about 43 and PEG about 2.9. The price is about 29.7x the 2026 EPS guide.
  - The average analyst target is about $546 (MarketBeat), roughly where the stock trades. Targets after earnings: Barclays 598, Evercore 575, UBS 570, JPMorgan 570, Truist 555, Piper Sandler 533.
  - Ratings are 1 Strong Buy, 11 Buy and 1 Hold. Barclays, UBS, Evercore and JPMorgan sit above the price, and Piper Sandler is the only one at or below it.
  - DCF-style sources call it overvalued (GuruFocus about $303), but those are low-weight sources.
- **Memory costs:** Direct memory spend went from about $50M in 2025 to about $150M in 2026, and could roughly double in 2027. Management plans selective price increases and still expects 2027 margin expansion.
- **Tariff refund:** About $70–75M of IEEPA tariff refund helped 2026 and will not recur in 2027.
- **Guidance size:** The full-year raise was smaller than the Q3 beat. Management called it "prudent," and an analyst noted the gap.
- **Insider selling:**
  - CEO Gregory Brown sold 40,500 shares on Nov 12 at 533.53 (about $21.6M), cutting his stake in half, to 40,500 shares.
  - He also sold about $6.9M on Sep 2, at 485.
  - These sales were at or near current prices. It is a mild negative signal, not proof of anything.
- **Leverage:**
  - Debt-to-equity is about 3.0. Long-term debt is $9.4B and short-term borrowings $750M.
  - A new $950M of senior notes funded D-Fend. Management targets net debt/EBITDA of about 2x at year-end.
- **Hytera:**
  - Motorola has recovered about $232M of the civil damages.
  - The criminal case was a partial disappointment in March: a $50M fine, with $290M restitution rejected.
  - About $116M tied to H-Series sales is still owed and under appeal.
  - This is a small, lumpy item and is excluded from non-GAAP results.
- **Competition:** Axon leads in body cameras, and Verkada competes in enterprise video. Share figures conflict, so I could not verify anything solid.

**Positioning and flows**
- Short interest was only 1.86% of float in late September and falling. Options skewed to calls, with a put/call ratio of 0.31 on Sep 25. These are stale readings, from before earnings.
- Volume was 2.1M on Nov 5 against a 1.06M average. Monday's 1.1x volume was unremarkable.
- Institutions own about 84%. Beta is about 0.86.
- Dividend is $1.21 a quarter (0.9% yield).

- **Catalyst timing:** The catalyst has already been priced in. The stock is up 16.4% in 20 sessions and now sits at consensus target, and the CEO sold into the move.

**Middleby (MIDD), research as of 12:55 AM CT, Tue 2026-11-17**

**Bottom line:** MIDD is now a smaller, cleaner commercial-foodservice company that just beat and raised, and the stock has re-rated about 30% off its October low. The fundamental story is good. The setup is extended after a fast run into a spot (141 to 148) where it has already stalled, and Monday's volume was thin. I found no scheduled company catalyst in the 1-10 session window.

**How the company changed in 2026**
- **Residential Kitchen (Viking, AGA and others):** 51% sold to 26North at an $885M valuation, closed Feb 2. Middleby got $564.6M net cash, kept 49% and took a $135M seller note. That note is mostly non-interest-bearing, due 2033, and carried at $84M.
- **Residential stake still hurts reported earnings:** the 49% stake lost $38.7M in Q3 ($67.6M over 9 months) under equity-method accounting. That is why GAAP EPS from continuing operations was $0.43 against adjusted $2.07. The carrying value is down to $73M. The filing doesn't say what drives the losses.
- **Food Processing:** spun off as Midera (ticker MFP) on July 6-7, one share for one. Middleby took a $233M dividend from it. MFP went from about $35 to the mid-$40s by early September.
- **Brewing:** being shut by year-end. It lost $27.7M at the operating line in Q3 and is expected to add about 40 bps to 2027 margin. Management said it is "not done shaping the portfolio" and may prune more brands.
- **Result:** a pure-play commercial foodservice company (Taylor ice and beverage, Pitco, Cooking and Warming) with a 2028 target of a 25-27% adjusted EBITDA margin, reaffirmed on the call.

**The Q3 report (Nov 5)**
- **Results:** sales were $652.6M, up 7.7% organically against a guide of about 4%. Adjusted EBITDA was $155.8M (23.9% margin, up 40 bps). Adjusted EPS was $2.07 against about $1.75 expected.
- **Raised 2026 guide:** adjusted EPS $7.13-7.29 (prior $6.73-6.89, consensus about $6.82), sales $2.519-2.534B, EBITDA $589-593M.
- **Q4 guide:** sales $621-635M, organic growth about 4.4% (a deceleration), adjusted EPS $1.76-1.92. Management called the trend "linear in a very positive direction."
- **Demand:**
  - Large quick-service chains drove growth, with beverage and ice platforms opening new dayparts. The Q3 call mentioned a global chain beverage program (a KFC example appears in one summary); I did not confirm the chain's name in the transcript.
  - International grew 14% and was 30% of sales, despite weakness in Asia and the Middle East.
  - The dealer channel was roughly flat against a strong prior-year comparison. Analysts probed this and the Q4 slowdown.
- **Margin drivers:** the August price increase starts flowing through in Q4. Lean programs at Taylor and Pitco are worth about 100 bps in 2027-28. Beverage investment is a roughly 100 bp drag now. Mix and inflation were headwinds. About $5M of tariff-refund (IEEPA) benefit helped Q3 and Q4's is immaterial, so Q3 quality is slightly flattered.
- **Capital allocation:** 1.0M shares bought in Q3 for $106.5M, 4.8M year to date (about 10% of the company), and about $76M more so far in Q4. Management says about 19% has been retired since 2025. **OPCH is a pending cash takeover, so the technical setup is not what drives the stock.** Shareholders get $32.05 in cash per share. The Monday close of 31.71 is a deal-spread price: 0.34 below the offer, about 1.1%. The "stretched, RSI 75" reading is just the stock sitting near the deal price. The 20-day range of 31.13 to 31.90 is a narrow band under the offer, and the recent 0.21x range compression fits that.

**Story to date**
- **Early 2026 collapse.** On April 30, Q1 revenue rose only about 1.3%, below the roughly $1.4B forecast. The 2026 revenue guide was cut from $5.8–6.0B to a midpoint of about $5.73B. The cause was weaker chronic inflammatory disease revenue, mainly fewer Stelara biosimilar patients converting than expected. The stock fell roughly 14–26% depending on the source. Securities-fraud "investigations" by law firms followed. These are not lawsuits. ([Yahoo](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/why-option-care-health-opch-031655815.html), [IndexBox](https://www.indexbox.io/blog/option-care-health-shares-tumble-26-on-weak-q1-2026-results-and-reduced-outlook/), [Investing.com transcript](https://www.investing.com/news/transcripts/earnings-call-transcript-option-care-healths-q1-2026-results-show-mixed-performance-93CH-4649925))
- **Deal announced Oct 6** (agreement signed Oct 5). Clayton, Dubilier & Rice (CD&R) and McKesson will buy the company for $32.05 cash, about $5.8B enterprise value. That is a roughly 42% premium to the $22.64 close on Oct 2 (about 37% against the Oct 5 close, per other sources). The stock jumped about 33%. After closing, CD&R would own about 51% and McKesson about 49%. ([Yahoo](https://finance.yahoo.com/healthcare/articles/option-care-health-agrees-5-144831242.html), [Bloomberg](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-10-06/mckesson-cd-r-to-buy-option-care-health-in-5-8-billion-deal), [Tikr](https://www.tikr.com/blog/option-care-health-soars-33-on-5-8-billion-buyout-by-cdr-and-mckesson-a-great-outcome))
- **Sale process, from the proxy's background section.**
  - The buyers opened at $28–32 on May 19, then bid $30, $31 and $32.05 in September.
  - They called $32.05 their "best and final."
  - A rival group, "Party J," indicated $30–34 on Sept 10 and $34 on Sept 22, but gave no signing timeline.
  - The buyers refused to match $34 or raise their price.
  - The company signed a 14-day exclusivity agreement and went ahead at $32.05.
  - The buyers refused a go-shop, so the deal has a no-shop with a fiduciary out.
  - Centerview gave a fairness opinion.
  - Takeaway: a higher rival indication existed and was passed over, which is a "price too low" argument for dissenters and for plaintiff firms. ([DEFM14A](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001014739/000114036126042547/ny20084196x2_defm14a.htm))
- **Q3 results, Nov 4.** Revenue was $1,493.5M, up 4.1%. Adjusted EBITDA was $124.6M, up 4.3%. Adjusted EPS was $0.49, in line. GAAP EPS was $0.38. There was no earnings call, and guidance was withdrawn because of the merger. ([HME News](https://www.hmenews.com/article/option-care-posts-4-1-increase-for-q3-withdraws-previous-guidance), [GuruFocus](https://www.gurufocus.com/news/9169242/option-care-health-reports-q3-2026-earnings-revenue-of-14935-million-beats-estimates-gaap-eps-at-038-misses-expectations), [TradingView](https://www.tradingview.com/news/stockstory:d6d985c3c094b:0-option-care-health-nasdaq-opch-posts-better-than-expected-sales-in-q3-2026/))
- **Analysts.** Ratings moved to neutral with the $32.05 deal price as the target. UBS cut its target from $39 to $32.05, and Morgan Stanley set $32.05. I found no November price targets. ([StockAnalysis](https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/opch/))

**Deal mechanics and risks (what actually matters for the next 1–10 sessions)**
- **Break protection.**
  - The buyers pay a reverse termination fee of $291.9M (6% of equity value) if they fail to close when required.
  - The company pays $146.0M if the deal ends over a superior proposal or a failed vote.
  - There is no financing condition. Committed debt is $3.15B of loans plus a $500M revolver, and equity commitments are about $2.87B.
  - The outside date is Oct 5, 2027.
- **Vote.** A special meeting is set for Dec 15, 2026, at 9 AM CT, virtual, with a Nov 3 record date. It needs a majority of all outstanding shares (about 149.8M), so abstentions and non-votes count against. The proxy is dated about Nov 9. I found no proxy-adviser (ISS or Glass Lewis) recommendation or organized opposition.
- **Antitrust.** The HSR filing was made Nov 3, with early termination requested. The 30-day waiting period is expected to end at 11:59 PM ET on Dec 3 unless there is early termination or a Second Request.
  - A Second Request would be the main negative event. I found none and no early-termination news.
  - State healthcare transaction notices and pharmacy licensure approvals are also required. A Massachusetts notice was received Nov 4.
  - McKesson is a large drug wholesaler, and one trade outlet noted growing lawmaker scrutiny of the big three wholesalers. I found no FTC-specific commentary.
- **Timing.** Both McKesson's 10-Q and the proxy say closing is expected in the first half of calendar 2027. The spread of about 1.1% is small for a roughly 3–7 month wait, so the market sees low risk.
- **Litigation.** There are no suits challenging the merger. The company has received one demand for books and records or supplemental disclosures. Several law firms announced price-and-process investigations. Expect nuisance suits and supplemental disclosures, which are normally harmless.

**Catalysts inside the window**
- **Dec 3 HSR expiry.** It is just past a 10-session window from Nov 17, so inside the window only an early-termination notice is likely. A Second Request announcement could come any time.
- **Dec 15 vote.** Also outside the window.
- **Possible rival bid.** The no-shop with a fiduciary out leaves a small chance of a topping bid, since Party J indicated $34. There was no sign of one in my searches.
- **Rare events.** These include supplemental-disclosure 8-Ks, a proxy-adviser recommendation, and state approvals.

**Read for the journal**
- **Upside is capped.** It is roughly $0.34 (1.1%) to the offer, plus a small tail if a topping bid emerges.
- **Downside is a fat tail.** A Second Request or an antitrust or vote failure could push the stock back toward the low-to-mid 20s. The unaffected price was $22.64, and the post-deal run-up was a re-rating.
- **Day-to-day movement is mostly spread-accrual noise.** ATR is 0.26. The stock sits well under the 52-week high of 36.80, which came before the April collapse. Momentum, trend and RSI carry essentially no information here.
- **It is not a swing-trade setup.** A stock in this position is merger-arbitrage paper, with a small gain against a large, rare loss.
- **Check before acting.** Early termination of the HSR waiting period, if granted, would be a clean positive. The Tuesday pre-market bid and ask should be looked at too, as after-hours was thin.

**Gaps.** I could not read the full proxy. The Centerview valuation ranges, the proxy's antitrust discussion and the full Background narrative past Oct 5 were beyond what I could retrieve. I found no news dated after about Nov 9, and I could not confirm any HSR outcome. Some search summaries disagreed on percentages and dates. The deal terms, vote date and HSR dates above come from the proxy and are the most reliable.

# CORT research brief (as of 12:55 AM CT, Tue 2026-11-17)

**Bottom line:** The 38% fall in 20 sessions is a fundamentals-and-sentiment repricing, not a single shock. Two events drove it: a competitor's ovarian cancer data on Oct 23, and a post-earnings slide that began Nov 4. Neither event damaged the numbers. Revenue and profit are at records. The stock gave back a speculative multiple, and there is no news after Nov 5 that explains the drift to 69. The next hard catalyst is the FDA decision on Cushing's syndrome on Dec 17, about 22 trading days away. That is probably outside a 1-10 session hold, but it will be anticipated.

## Background
- **Dec 31, 2025:** The FDA issued a complete response letter (CRL) for relacorilant in Cushing's syndrome. The stock fell about 50% to the high-$20s to low-$30s. The 52-week low is 28.66. Truist cut its target to $50 but kept Buy ([TradingView/Invezz](https://www.tradingview.com/news/invezz:0ccf2730a094b:0-why-corcept-therapeutics-stock-crashed-today-and-what-comes-next/)).
- **Mar 25, 2026:** The FDA approved Lifyorli (relacorilant plus nab-paclitaxel) in platinum-resistant ovarian cancer, 3.5 months early. The label requires one to three prior regimens, including bevacizumab. It is the first selective glucocorticoid receptor antagonist. The list price is $37,900 per 28-day cycle. The trial was ROSELLA (381 patients): overall survival 16.0 vs 11.9 months ([Business Wire](https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260325948774/en/FDA-Approves-Corcepts-Selective-Glucocorticoid-Receptor-Antagonist-Lifyorli-relacorilant-Plus-Nab-Paclitaxel-for-Treatment-of-Patients-with-Platinum-Resistant-Ovarian-Cancer), [Pharmaceutical Technology](https://www.pharmaceutical-technology.com/news/corcept-therapeutics-lifyorli-relacorilant-fda-approval-ovarian-cancer/)). A director bought 100k shares at $33.14 on Mar 17. The stock ran from about $34 to a 126 high, so it roughly tripled by autumn.
- **Jun 17:** Corcept resubmitted the Cushing's application. After the CRL, the FDA asked for one specific global statistical analysis covering glucose, weight and blood pressure endpoints, with no new trial. The target action date is **Dec 17, 2026** ([Q3 call, Motley Fool](https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/11/04/corcept-therapeutics-cort-q3-2026-earnings-call-transcript/)).
- **Jul 27:** Wolfe Research downgraded to Underperform with a $50 target. Its argument is that the price already assumes a successful resubmission, limited generic erosion and favorable legal outcomes ([MarketBeat](https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/wolfe-research-reiterates-underperform-rating-for-corcept-therapeutics-nasdaqcort-2026-07-27/)). Guidance was raised in July to $1.1-1.2B.
- **Aug-Oct:** Insiders sold about $43M over 90 days, including directors at $118-123 ([MarketBeat](https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/estimates-cort-stock-earnings-estimates-decreased-by-hc-wainwright-2026-11-05/)). The Oct 5 close was 122.03.

## The 20-day leg down (about 112 to 69)
1. **Oct 5-22:** The stock slid from 122 to about 107 (derived: 85.86 close after a -20.1% day implies roughly 107 beforehand). Trefis cites no specific cause ([Trefis](https://www.trefis.com/stock/cort/articles/620463/can-corcept-therapeutics-stock-rally-40-after-this-dip/2026-10-26)).
2. **Oct 23, the main shock (-20.1% to 85.86):** Genmab's Phase 3 RAINFOL-02 of Rina-S (an antibody-drug conjugate) in platinum-resistant ovarian cancer hit both endpoints. That is the same patient setting as Lifyorli. The numbers were PFS HR 0.29 and OS HR 0.43 against investigator's-choice chemotherapy, in 584 patients ([Chemxplore](https://chemxplore.com/news/rinatabart-sesutecan-platinum-resistant-ovarian-cancer), [Investing.com](https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/why-is-corcept-therapeutics-stock-tumbling-today-93CH-4970122)). William Blair called it highly competitive with Elahere. I recall ROSELLA's hazard ratios being much weaker (roughly 0.7), but that is from memory and I did not verify it here. Cross-trial comparisons are loose, since the comparator arms differ and Rina-S is an ADC. Genmab has not given medians, a filing timeline or a meeting date. Full data are still to come, and that is a possible further overhang.
3. **Nov 3 (earnings, after the close):** The quarter was strong ([8-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001088856/000162828026069494/cort110326ex991pressrelease.htm)).
   - Revenue was $340.5M, up 64% year over year, against about $324-339M expected.
   - Korlym plus its authorized generic was $249.1M, up 19% from Q2.
   - Lifyorli was $91.4M, up 92% from Q2.
   - Diluted EPS was $1.01 vs about $0.84 expected.
   - Cash was $662M, up $118M in the quarter. About $44M went to buybacks.
   - Guidance was only **reiterated** at $1.1-1.2B. Nine-month revenue is $761.5M, so hitting the midpoint implies roughly $389M in Q4 (a third-party calculation).
   - The stock closed at 81.93 that day and slipped after hours.
4. **Nov 4 (-8.6% to 74.88):** The likely causes are no guidance raise, and management declining to engage on Rina-S data. An analyst's question on Korlym price erosion got no direct answer ([Alphastreet](https://news.alphastreet.com/corcept-therapeutics-cort-drops-8-6-to-74-88/), [Motley Fool transcript](https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/11/04/corcept-therapeutics-cort-q3-2026-earnings-call-transcript/)). Management said "none of these drugs are curing this disease" and floated combinations with ADCs. It also gave no label detail on the Cushing's review. The stock dipped below its 200-day average on Nov 5, near 71.6.
5. **Nov 5-16:** There was no identified news. Daily closes were about 74 on Nov 10, about 73 on Nov 13 and 69.58 on Nov 16 (quote-page figure; your 69.22 is the one to use). This looks like drift and technical selling. I found no cause for Monday's -5.1% or Friday's -4.6%.

## Other facts
- **Insiders:** Executives sold at $81-82 on Nov 2-3 (two officers, about $2.7M). A director sold 1,500 shares at $74.07 on Nov 10. These are small and look like routine or planned sales, but the timing right before earnings adds a mild negative tone ([MarketBeat](https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/price-corcept-therapeutics-nasdaq-cort-stock-price-crosses-below-200-day-moving-average-on-insider-selling-2026-11-05/), [MarketBeat, Nov 13](https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/insider-corcept-therapeutics-nasdaq-cort-stock-insider-daniel-swisher-jr-sells-1500-shares-2026-11-13/)).
- **Analysts (MarketBeat count: 5 Buy, 2 Hold, 1 Sell):**
  - Piper Sandler raised its target to $173 after earnings.
  - HC Wainwright is at $165, Truist at $164 and Canaccord at $150.
  - Wolfe is the lone bear at $50.
  - I found no post-Oct 23 downgrades beyond a Zacks move to hold.
  - The sell side has not capitulated, so there is no capitulation signal.
- **Valuation:** Market cap is about $7.5B at 69. The trailing P/E was about 57 near 73. Trefis noted trailing operating margin had compressed to 0.8% at the June quarter, though Q3 operating income was $114.7M. SG&A was up 33% year over year with the launch.
- **Teva antitrust case:** Trial is set for March 2027. Judge Wise denied most of the motion to dismiss. Corcept's summary-judgment motion was filed in October and Teva's opposition on about Nov 7, so a ruling could land anytime ([MLex](https://www.mlex.com/mlex/articles/2547628), [PYMNTS](https://www.pymnts.com/cpi-posts/corcept-seeks-to-block-ex-judges-testimony-in-teva-antitrust-fight/)). Insurers (Aetna and others) have filed similar claims. A summary-judgment ruling is a two-sided event risk inside the window. The Federal Circuit affirmed non-infringement of the Korlym patents in February, and rehearing was denied in July, so the patent fight is over. Teva's generic has been on the market since January 2024. The 10-Qs are at the [SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001088856/000162828026050613/cort-20260630.htm).
- **Pipeline:** The EU CHMP gave a positive opinion in September, with European Commission approval expected by year-end. That is a minor catalyst. Miricorilant (MASH) and dazucorilant (ALS, exploratory data, Phase 3 planned for 2027) are background only. Oncology readouts are all due by the end of 2027.
- **Management's long-term claims:** At least $1B a year from Lifyorli, and $3-5B total by 2030 if Cushing's is approved.

## Read for a 1-10 session trade

agents.report:
OPCH is a pending cash take-private at $32.05 per share, so the stock is trading as a merger-arbitrage instrument and not on its fundamentals. At 31.71 it sits 0.34 below the offer, a 1.1% gross spread.

**What happened**
- **Timeline:** Option Care Health ran a sale process through 2025 and 2026.
  - Early 2025: CD&R and three other sponsors signed NDAs but made no proposals.
  - May 19, 2026: CD&R and McKesson proposed $28–32.
  - September 10–11: the board got indications of $30–34 from a "Party J Consortium", $29–31 from "Party K", and $30 from the CD&R/McKesson group, which raised its bid to $31.
  - September 17: CD&R/McKesson made a "best and final" offer of $32.05, conditioned on two weeks of exclusivity.
  - September 22: Party J indicated $34 but gave no timeline. The exclusivity terms stopped the company from engaging with it.
  - The CD&R/McKesson group refused a go-shop (a post-signing window to solicit rival bids).
  - Signed October 5, announced October 6. The stock jumped about 33% on the news, with roughly 22 times normal volume.
- **Terms:**
  - Enterprise value is about $5.8B. The premium is about 37% to the October 5 close, or about 42% against the price a few days earlier.
  - CD&R takes about 51% and McKesson about 49%, putting in roughly $1.4B. McKesson gets a framework to buy CD&R's stake later.
  - The company stays a standalone business under its current management.
- **Deal protections:**
  - No go-shop. A no-shop applies, with a fiduciary out before the vote.
  - Company break fee is $146M, about 3.0% of equity value. Parent reverse fee is $292M, about 6.0%.
  - There is no financing condition. Committed debt is $3.15B in loans plus a $500M revolver. Equity commitments are about $2.87B.
- **Rival bid:** The $34 Party J indication is the one fact that could still produce a higher bid. The proxy says the board weighed that bidder's price and whether it could actually close. The deal terms bar the company from soliciting offers. William Blair and Barrington analysts said a topping bid looked unlikely, and I found no reporting of any rival bid.
- **Operating picture:**
  - Q3 (reported November 4, with no call) had revenue of $1,493.5M (+4.1%), adjusted EBITDA of $124.6M (+4.3%), and adjusted EPS of $0.49 (+8.9%). GAAP EPS of $0.38 missed the $0.46 consensus.
  - Guidance is withdrawn.
  - The earlier weakness came from Stelara biosimilar pressure and a guidance cut in May.
  - The long-range plan was reworked for Inflation Reduction Act drug pricing, biosimilars, and payor and pharmacy-benefit-manager dynamics.
- **Analyst and legal reaction:** Citizens downgraded the stock on the deal and William Blair moved to Market Perform. Ademi and Halper Sadeh announced fair-price investigations, which are routine, and I found no actual lawsuit.

**Upcoming dates**
- Both parties filed HSR on November 3 and asked for early termination. The 30-day waiting period ends at 11:59 PM ET on December 3 unless a Second Request is issued.
- State healthcare and pharmacy approvals are also required.
- Stockholder vote is December 15, 2026, at 9:00 AM CT. Approval needs a majority of all outstanding shares (about 149.8M as of the record date), and abstentions count as no. Insiders hold about 0.86%.
- Outside date is October 5, 2027. Company guidance for closing is the first half of 2027.

**What this means for the screen and a 1–10 session trade**
- **Screen signals:** RSI 75, being stretched, and the lack of a turn describe a stock grinding up toward a fixed price. They don't predict a reversal. The tight range (0.21x), low volume, and flat after-hours price fit a pinned arb stock.
- **Upside:** The upside is capped near 0.34 (1.1%) unless a topping bid appears.
- **Downside:**
  - A Second Request, a failed vote, or financing or antitrust trouble could break the spread.
  - If the deal broke, the pre-deal price was about $23.40 (implied from the 37% premium). That is roughly a 25% drop against a 1% gain.
  - A deal this size with state approvals pending has a long path before closing.
- **Near-term catalysts:**
  - Early termination of the HSR waiting period, or its expiry on December 3, would narrow the spread. That date is about 12 sessions out, so it is likely just outside a 1–10 session window.
  - A Second Request would widen it.
  - The vote on December 15 is outside the window.
  - A proxy-advisor recommendation could land at any time. I found none yet.
- **Not checked:** I did not find a live spread or any news from November 10–16 beyond the filings above.

agents.report:
**ONE Gas (OGS): research for the 1-10 session decision, as of 12:40 AM CT Tue 2026-11-17**

**Bottom line.** OGS is a steady regulated gas utility. Its recent rise has a clear cause: a Q3 beat and raise on Nov 2, plus a data-center and large-load story. The next known catalyst is the 2027 and five-year guidance in early December, probably outside a 1-10 session window. Management has already warned that 2027 growth will be below trend. That makes the stretched, no-turn setup look like a drift into a known event, not a fresh catalyst.

**What the company is**
- It is a pure-play natural gas distribution utility, serving about 2.3M customers in Oklahoma (Oklahoma Natural Gas, ONG), Kansas (Kansas Gas Service) and Texas (Texas Gas Service).
- It trades on regulated rate base growth, with a $0.68 quarterly dividend (about 3.3% yield).

**Q3 report and guidance (Nov 2, release; call Nov 3)**
- Adjusted EPS was $0.53 against $0.47 a year earlier, versus a $0.48 Zacks consensus.
- Revenue was $391M. Sources conflict on whether that beat or missed: one cites a $360M consensus, another $398M.
- 2026 adjusted EPS guidance went to $4.95-$5.01 from $4.89-$4.95. This is the second raise this year, and the midpoint is now $4.98.
- Texas House Bill 4384, which cuts regulatory lag, is now worth about $0.45 of 2026 EPS, up from $0.35. Flat operating costs also helped.
- Year to date, weather was 23% warmer than normal, but weather-normalization mechanisms offset it.
- Capex is about $800M for 2026. The 2026 financing plan is complete: $375M of 5.45% notes due 2036 were issued in August. Management says no more 2026 equity is needed, and forward-sale agreements for 2026 are at about $82 a share.
- Rate changes already in place: the Kansas surcharge (about $14.3M) took effect in October, and the Texas reliability filing ($36.9M) took effect in July.
- Oklahoma: the Corporation Commission approved the performance-based rate change on Oct 14. It adds $28.7M a year, with interim rates in effect since June 26.

**Large loads and data centers**
- Four projects are signed, worth about $22M of annual revenue and $200M of capital. They include an Oklahoma City data center due to start soon, an El Paso manufacturing site, a company-funded Texas LNG project (service Q1 2027) and a 43-mile pipeline for a Western Farmers gas plant (due Q3 2028).
- Eight late-stage projects represent about 3 GW and up to 1 Bcf/day of demand, with 20 more in early evaluation.
- Management declined to give capital figures for those until commercial negotiations conclude. These figures are for the December update.

**Known catalyst and risks**
- **December plan:** 2027 guidance and updated 5-year guidance come in "early December," followed by New York conferences in the second week of December.
- **Below-trend 2027:** The Oklahoma performance-based mechanism ends and a longer general rate case comes in 2027. Management also wants to address a higher cost of capital in that filing.
- **Long-term target:** The 5-7% adjusted EPS growth target is unchanged, now rebased on $4.98. An analyst asked about a prior reference to about $6 EPS by 2030, and management would not confirm it.
- **Equity:** Management says large-load capital needs and outperformance offset each other, so the 2027-2030 equity range is unchanged. The net shows up in the December plan.
- **Rate sensitivity:** A 100 bp move in Fed funds is worth about $0.09 of EPS. Utilities fell on Nov 10 as Treasury yields rose (a Dow Jones roundup, no yield levels given).
- **Oklahoma legal and political risk:** Two legislators, Reps. Gann and West, have eleven or more appeals pending at the Oklahoma Supreme Court against Corporation Commission rulings. They target Winter Storm Uri securitization (ONG's $1.36B of bonds) and past ONG rate cases.
  - The commissioner vote and ethics allegations are the legislators' claims, not findings.
  - The June appeal over the 2026 rate case drew a show-cause order on whether the order was appealable. I could not confirm that the Oct 14 order is under appeal. One source and the company's release say it is; I found no news or docket confirmation. I found no ruling.
  - This is a tail risk. A surprise docket ruling could move the stock.
- **Ex-dividend:** The record date was Nov 16 (ex-date reported as Nov 16), payable Dec 3. A $0.68 drop is already reflected in Monday's price, if the ex-date was Nov 16.

**Analysts and price context**
- There are 13 analysts: 7 Buy and 6 Hold. The average target is $87.12, about 3.7% above $84.
- Post-earnings moves: Mizuho $90 (from $89), Scotiabank $87 (from $86), Wells Fargo $86 (from $85, equal weight), and BTIG Buy at $95.
- Pre-earnings: Morgan Stanley cut its target to $78 (equal weight) on Oct 21.
- I could not verify a reported Jefferies October downgrade to Hold with a $103 to $80 target. It is undated in the results, and one tracker shows a $76 target.
- Price at 84 sits right at the average target, with the stock already above Wells Fargo's $86 minus 2%, and in range of the Scotiabank, Mizuho and BTIG targets.
- The stock opened at $82.22 on Nov 4 (Defense World, MarketBeat). It hit an earlier 2026 high near $88-90 in March-April. One source lists a 52-week high of $90.78, versus your 89.27 (possibly an intraday versus close difference).
- Institutional buying (CenterBook, Aberdeen) is only routine 13F filing news.
- I found no insider transaction data, no short interest figures, and no news dated Nov 12-16 beyond routine filings.

**For the journal.** The story is a clean fundamental beat plus an AI-power demand angle for a gas utility, but 84 is near the average target. The next scheduled information is early December, with the dividend already out. Expect rate and yield moves and sector rotation to dominate the next 1-10 sessions. Watch the 10-year yield, and the 20-day high of 84.65 as the first test.
